itinerary.title: Welcome to Japan- Arrival in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Welcome to Japan! 

Our staff will be waiting for you at Haneda/Narita Airport. 
We will provide you with everything you need for this trip and escort you to the taxi/bus stand or train station.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Sightseeing in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Asakusa→This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
★TOKYO SKYTREE®→A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
★The Imperial Palace→A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
★Shibuya Scramble Crossing→A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
★Harajuku→An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Kyoto + sightseeing in Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. This will help you explore Kyoto more easily. 

Travel from Tokyo Station to Kyoto by Shinkansen in the morning.
🚅Tokyo Station→Kyoto Station

 Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>  *Entrance fees not included
★Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka→ Capture countless photos along Kyoto’s charming traditional streets.
★Kiyomizu-dera Temple→ Take in panoramic views of the city from one of Kyoto’s most celebrated temples. Stay a little longer to enjoy an unforgettable sunset.
★Gion and Yasaka Shrine→Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
★Stroll along the Kamo River→This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Sightseeing in Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Today, we will take a longer trip to explore Kyoto’s famous sights.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Kinkaku-ji Temple→A beautiful World Heritage site that is gold-plated.
★Arashiyama→A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
★Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine→A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
★Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi→An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Osaka + sightseeing in Osaka
itinerary.description:
Hotel Check out
Take train to Osaka (In the morning) (using an IC Card Suica)
🚃Kyoto Station→Osaka Station

Osaka is a lively city known for its busy downtown areas and varied food culture. It has many attractions, from historical sites to modern viewpoints.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>  *Entrance fees not included
★Tennoji & Abeno Harukas→Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
★Shinsekai→Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.
★Umeda Sky Building (Sky Garden Observatory)→Visit this observation deck for 360-degree views of Osaka. The night view is especially beautiful.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Sightseeing in Osaka
itinerary.description:
Day 2 in Osaka: More Tourist Spots to Explore!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Nakanoshima Area→Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks. We recommend visiting the art museum and the Osaka City Central Public Hall.
★Osaka Castle→Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
★Dotonbori & Shinsaibashi→Explore this busy district famous for its bright signs and street food. Be sure to try local dishes like takoyaki.

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for spending the last 7 days with our tour.  We hope to see you again!

tour.title: Historic Towns & Mountain Heritage
tour.subtitle: Budget-Friendly Travel in Tokyo, Takayama & Kyoto
tour.description: Experience the best of Japan at an unbeatable value. This 7-day self-guided tour takes you through Japan's most captivating destinations—Tokyo, Takayama, Shirakawa-go, and Kyoto—with Shinkansen tickets, hotel stays, and luggage delivery all included. Start in Tokyo, where ancient temples meet neon-lit streets. Then journey into the Japanese Alps to Takayama, a beautifully preserved Edo-period town famous for its wooden streetscapes and melt-in-your-mouth Hida beef. From there, visit the UNESCO World Heritage village of Shirakawa-go, where traditional thatched-roof farmhouses stand against a breathtaking mountain backdrop. Finally, explore Kyoto, the cultural heart of Japan, with its iconic temples, bamboo groves, and atmospheric geisha districts. With all major logistics taken care of, you're free to explore at your own pace—no rigid schedules, no group tours. Just you, Japan, and the freedom to discover.

itinerary.description:

★ Omotesando Shopping Street → Enjoy local foods such as momiji manju (maple leaf-shaped sweets) and fresh oysters.

After sightseeing, take the ferry back to Hiroshima City and continue sighseeing.

- Okage Yokocho: This street has buildings from the Edo and Meiji periods. You can try local dishes like Ise udon and Akafuku mochi.

After visiting, take a local bus to Ujiyamada, then transfer to Kyoto by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Discover More of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Let's continue to discover the charms of Tokyo.

- Meiji Jingu Shrine: Take a leisurely stroll at the largest shrine in Tokyo!
- Omotesando: Perhaps a relaxing cup of coffee to be enjoyed in the afternoon?

itinerary.title: Morning in Himeji and Journey to Hiroshima
itinerary.description:
Check out the Hotel and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore Himeji and Hiroshima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Himeji by Shinkansen.

Himeji is a beautiful castle town with rich history.
Enjoy sightseeing in Himeji!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Himeji Castle: Admire the beauty of a UNESCO World Heritage Site of Himeji Castle and be sure not to miss the spectacular nighttime illumination.
- Koko-en: This Japanese garden located on the west side of Himeji Castle is a beautifully designed space established on the site of a former Edo-period mansion. Visitors can appreciate the garden’s seasonal landscapes, and matcha tasting is also offered for an authentic cultural experience.

In the afternoon, travel from Himeji to Hiroshima by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Miyajima & the Sacred Shrine by the Sea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Travel to Miyajima by ferry.

Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an "island of the gods."
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- The of Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry.

itinerary.title: Reflecting on Hiroshima's history, then Transfer to Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions.
Let's spend more time exploring Hiroshima.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): A UNESCO World Heritage Site representing the impact of war.
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.

In the afternoon, travel from Hiroshima to Kyoto by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Exploring Kyoto's Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Pontocho: Wander this lantern-lit alley by the Kamo River, lined with charming machiya-style restaurants and bars.
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Let's continue to discover the charms of Kyoto.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.

itinerary.title: Beyond the Capital: Modern Flavors or Timeless History
itinerary.description:
Ready to explore beyond Kyoto? 

Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Love gourmet food and shopping? 
Osaka is the place to go. Shop at Osaka's foremost shopping districts Dotonbori and Tsutenkaku Tower and indulge in takoyaki and okonomiyaki until your heart's content!
- Want to see more ancient history? 
Nara is the place to be. Nara predates Kyoto as an ancient capital, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Todaiji Temple, Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and Kofukuji Temple — are just some of many spots with a rich and immersive history.
Nara Park also provides a unique experience where feeding the gentle deer offers a moment to connect with nature.

itinerary.title: Head to Hakone and explore at your own pace
itinerary.description:
Check out the Hotel and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Hakone at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Odawara by Shinkansen, then take the local train to Hakone-Yumoto.

Hakone is a popular hot spring destination in Japan, known for its views of Mount Fuji and great dining.
Enjoy sightseeing in Hakone!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Hakone Open-Air Museum: Art in the natural landscape.
- Owakudani: Volcanic area with steaming vents and black eggs.
- Togendai: Lunch with views of Lake Ashi and Mount Fuji.
- Lake Ashi: Enjoy beautiful nature and Mount Fuji.
- The Old Highway Cedar Avenue: Lined with historic cedar trees.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel
Relax in the hot springs to unwind

itinerary.title: Back to Tokyo and Continue Exploring
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Travel from Hakone-Yumoto to Odawara by local train, then transfer to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

Let's enjoy a half-day in Tokyo.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?
Here are some great spots to check out.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for joining the 13-day tour!
We look forward to seeing you again.

tour.description: Embark on a 13-day journey through Japan’s diverse landscapes and cultural treasures. Begin in dynamic Tokyo, then relax in Hakone’s hot springs with views of Mt. Fuji. Continue to lively Osaka, famous for its street food and vibrant atmosphere, before heading into the Japanese Alps to discover Takayama’s preserved old town. Visit Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, known for its traditional thatched-roof farmhouses, and explore Inuyama, home to one of Japan’s oldest original castles. Conclude your adventure back in Tokyo, enriched with memories of Japan’s history, tradition, and natural beauty.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After you check out, take the local train from Hakone-Yumoto to Odawara, then transfer to Shin-Osaka by Shinkansen.

Osaka is a lively city known for its busy downtown areas and varied food culture. It has many attractions, from historical sites to modern viewpoints.
Enjoy sightseeing in Osaka.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Dotonbori & Shinsaibashi: Enjoy bright signs and street food like takoyaki.
- Umeda Sky Building: Visit the observatory for a 360-degree view of Osaka, especially beautiful at night.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Making Memories at Universal City
itinerary.description:
We recommend spending time at Universal City to enjoy its world-class theme park. It’s packed with attractions based on Hollywood movies and popular video games, along with entertainment where you can meet beloved characters. Thrills, excitement, and smiles await.

Enjoy a fun-filled day at the theme park in Universal City, Osaka!

itinerary.title: Free Exploration of Vibrant Osaka
itinerary.description:
Why don't you explore more tourist spots in Osaka?
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

itinerary.title: Beyond Osaka: Scenic Beauty or Ancient Traditions
itinerary.description:
Ready to explore beyond Osaka?

Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Love culture and scenery?
Kyoto is the place to be. As Japan’s former imperial capital, Kyoto is home to countless historic temples, shrines, and traditional streetscapes. Explore iconic spots such as Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine, and Arashiyama, where you can experience the timeless beauty and culture of Japan.
- Want to see more ancient history?
Nara is the place to be. Nara predates Kyoto as an ancient capital, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Todaiji Temple, Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and Kofukuji Temple — are just some of many spots with a rich and immersive history.
Nara Park also provides a unique experience where feeding the gentle deer offers a moment to connect with nature.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Check out the Hotel and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Takayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Shin-Osaka to Nagoya by Shinkansen, then take the limited express train to Takayama.

Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.

Enjoy sightseeing in Takayama.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takayama Jinya: This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
- Old Town (Sanmachi Street): This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.
- Hida no Sato: This is an open-air museum featuring traditional Gassho style houses. Visitors can experience the original Japanese landscape of Gassho-zukuri farmhouses.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go: Thatched Roof Villages
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

Take a chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: From Mountain Charm to Timeless Castles
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the afternoon, travel from Takayama to Unuma by limited express and local train, then transfer to Inuyamayuen by limited express train.

Inuyama Castle is a National Treasure and one of Japan's oldest original castles. It offers great views from its historic tower.

In the afternoon, travel from Inuyama to Meitetsu Nagoya by limited express train, then transfer to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

tour.description: Discover Japan’s cultural and World Heritage treasures on this 13-day tour. From vibrant Tokyo to the preserved streets of Takayama and the thatched farmhouses of Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, then visit Inuyama Castle, a designated National Treasure. Explore Kyoto’s timeless beauty, then continue to Himeji Castle, one of Japan’s most spectacular UNESCO World Heritage Sites, and note the differences in style and history between these iconic castles. Travel onward to Hiroshima and the sacred island of Miyajima, before returning to Tokyo. A journey through Japan’s history, tradition, and iconic landmarks.

Visit Japan's top entertainment theme park in the Tokyo Bay area. 

Experience an amazing world where all ages can immerse themselves in the story, with beautifully designed streets, various attractions, and seasonal displays. 

At a park, you’ll find a castle and enjoy classic rides and parades. The other park, themed around the sea, offers exciting scenery and enjoyable rides for both adults and children.

Be sure to visit the park today and have a magical time!

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we suggest visiting a different park with a new theme that you didn’t see yesterday. Each park gives you a unique experience and charm.

You can also explore Tokyo’s urban attractions, including historic streets and shopping areas.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Universal City, Osaka. You can explore Nagoya at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Maihama to Tokyo by local train, then transfer to Nagoya by Shinkansen.

Nagoya is a beautiful city full of samurai history and unique food.
Enjoy sightseeing in Nagoya!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nagoya Castle: This is the symbol of Nagoya, known for its golden shachihoko ornaments.
- Noritake Forest: Here, you can learn about the history of ceramics and craftsmanship.
- Osu Shopping District: Explore this lively area, which combines old shops with a youthful vibe.

itinerary.title: Brick Theme Park & Japanese Animation World Experience
itinerary.description:

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Ai･chikyuhaku Kinen Koen Station: This park is full of nature and allows you to experience Japan's famous animated works. You can walk through areas that look like the settings from these stories and feel like you are part of them.
- Nagoya Port area: This outdoor park recreates the world of a famous brick toy, with colorful streets and various attractions.

itinerary.title: Making Memories at Universal City, Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

We recommend spending time at Universal City to enjoy its world-class theme park. It’s packed with attractions based on Hollywood movies and popular video games, along with entertainment where you can meet beloved characters. Thrills, excitement, and smiles await.

Enjoy a fun-filled day at the theme park in Universal City, Osaka!

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Where Movie Magic Comes to Life

Breakfast at the hotel

The adventure continues — let's dive back into the magic!

The park features areas recreating movie worlds and famous works, along with thrilling attractions that offer exciting entertainment for all ages.

Enjoy sightseeing in Osaka!

itinerary.title: Guided Tokyo Discovery & Japan Life Experience Day
Visiting Ise, the Spiritual Heart of Japan
Choose Your Ise Adventure Day
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, please choose one of the two activities below that interests you the most.

[A] Minami-Ise Fishing Village Fishing Experience Tour  
Cook salt-baked fish caught in Asoura, a traditional fishing village. You will also tour a fish farm with local fishermen. Enjoy fishing in the waters of Minami-Ise. 

[B] Shima Green Adventure and Ama Hut Tour  
Get active and explore the natural forest. This option is great for families with young children. For lunch, you will experience the ama culture, which has been part of Ise for over 2,000 years. An Ise ama will grill fish right in front of you.

After the activities, return to the hotel.
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Ninja Training Experience in Iga
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the afternoon, travel from Kashikojima to Nabari by limited express train, then take a chartered taxi to Akame.

Akame is a tranquil mountain retreat, where lush forests, beautiful waterfalls, and fascinating ninja history come together.
Enjoy sightseeing in Akame.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Akame 48 Falls: Hike through lush forests and along peaceful streams, discovering a series of beautiful waterfalls along the way.
- Ninja Training Village: Step into the world of ninja and try your hand at traditional ninja skills through fun, hands-on activities.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Nabari, then transfer to Kyoto by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Exploring Kyoto's Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Pontocho: Wander this lantern-lit alley by the Kamo River, lined with charming machiya-style restaurants and bars.
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Let's continue to discover the charms of Kyoto.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.

itinerary.title: Beyond the Capital: Modern Flavors or Timeless History
itinerary.description:
Ready to explore beyond Kyoto?

Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Love gourmet food and shopping?
Osaka is the place to go. Shop at Osaka's foremost shopping districts Dotonbori and Tsutenkaku Tower and indulge in takoyaki and okonomiyaki until your heart's content!
For a change of pace, why not visit Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan and discover the fascinating world beneath the sea?
- Want to see more ancient history?
Nara is the place to be. Nara predates Kyoto as an ancient capital, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Todaiji Temple, Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and Kofukuji Temple — are just some of many spots with a rich and immersive history.
Nara Park also provides a unique experience where feeding the gentle deer offers a moment to connect with nature.

itinerary.title: Sayonara – Until We Meet Again in Japan!

The tour ends at hotel check-out.

We look forward to seeing you again.

itinerary.title: Toba's Ama diving culture and the delicious seafood
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Nagoya to Toba by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

Toba is a port town in Mie Prefecture. It is known for its beautiful sea and island views and for its Ama diving culture.

From Toba, take the shuttle bus to Hachiman Kamado.  
Hachiman Kamado is an Ama hut where you can enjoy a meal while Ama divers share stories about their fishing experiences and lives. You will enjoy delicious Ise seafood for lunch!

After lunch, take the shuttle bus back to Toba, then travel from Toba to Kashikojima by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in  
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, board the Kashikojima España Cruise, and take in the full beauty of Ago Bay. 

Around noon, travel from Kashikojima to Toba by limited express train.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Mikimoto Pearl Island: This is where the first successful pearl cultivation happened. Here, you can learn about the history of pearl farming. Watch live demonstrations by Ama divers  and shop for beautiful pearl jewelry.

Travel from Toba to Osaka Namba by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

itinerary.title: Day trip to Koyasan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the spiritual center of Shingon Buddhism
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

In the morning, travel from Nankai Naｍba to Gokurakubashi by limited express train, and then transfer to Koyasan by cable car.

Koyasan is a mountain town recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. 
It is surrounded by cedar forests and has deep ties to Japanese Buddhism. Kobo Daishi Kukai practiced asceticism here for over 1,200 years. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Danjo Garan: This is the main area of Koyasan. You can see the famous Konpon Daito Pagoda and Kondo Hall here, which create a beautiful landscape.
- Strolling the Approach: Walk through the calm mountain town, which has souvenir shops and stores that sell Buddhist altar goods.
- Kongobuji Temple: This is the main temple of Koyasan Shingon Buddhism. It features one of Japan’s largest rock gardens, perfect for quiet reflection.

In the evening, return to Nankai Namba by  cable car and limited express train.

itinerary.title: Discovering the Timeless Charm of Nara and transfer to Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Nara and Kyoto at your leisure.
In the morning, travel from Osaka to Nara by Sightseeing Limited Express "AONIYOSHI", or another limited express train.

Nara is one of Japan's oldest cultural centers, filled with ancient temples, historic shrines, and peaceful parks.
Enjoy sightseeing in Nara!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Todai-ji Temple: The Daibutsuden Hall, home to the Great Buddha, is an impressive sight where you can experience the history and religious culture of Japan.
- Kasuga Taisha Shrine: Characterized by its vermilion-colored structures and more than a thousand stone lanterns. 
- Kofuku-ji Temple: A historic temple featuring a graceful five-story pagoda.
- Nara Park: A vast park blending serene scenery with historic landmarks. Take a moment to interact with and feed the gentle deer that inhabit this unique area.

Transfer to Kyoto by limited express train.

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>

Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?

Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>

Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: The adventure kicks off in vibrant Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: The Timeless Charm of Kanazawa
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore Kanazawa at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Kanazawa by Shinkansen.

Kanazawa is a city that keeps the feel of an Edo-period castle town while also featuring modern art and architecture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kanazawa!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Higashi Chaya District: Enjoy a magical atmosphere. It’s a great place for a stroll. 
- Korinbo/Katamachi Area: This lively district is perfect for dining. Try local dishes like seafood and oden.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Kanazawa: Gardens, Arts & Samurai Heritage
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kanazawa.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Omi-cho Market: Visit this market to enjoy local food, especially fresh seafood.
- Kenroku-en Garden: Explore one of Japan's Three Great Gardens, which offers beautiful views in every season.
- Kanazawa Castle Park: This park, next to Kenroku-en, has castle ruins and a large area to walk around.
- 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art: Check out this museum that showcases contemporary art, making it a great stop during your city walk.

itinerary.title: Exploring Kyoto’s Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Kanazawa to Tsuruga by Shinkansen,  then take the limited express train to Kyoto.

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.
 
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Let's explore beyond Kyoto!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Kyoto? 
Here are some great spots to check out

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Love gourmet food and shopping? 
Osaka is the place to go. Shop at Osaka's foremost shopping districts Dotonbori and Tsutenkaku Tower and indulge in takoyaki and okonomiyaki until your heart's content!
- Want to see more ancient history? 
Nara is the place to be. Nara predates Kyoto as an ancient capital, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Todaiji Temple, Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and Kofukuji Temple — are just some of many spots with a rich and immersive history.
Nara Park also provides a unique experience where feeding the gentle deer offers a moment to connect with nature.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Takayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Nagoya by Shinkansen, then take the limited express train to Takayama. 

Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Takayama.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takayama Jinya: This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
- Old Town (Sanmachi Street): This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.
- Hida no Sato: This is an open-air museum featuring traditional Gassho style houses. Visitors can experience the original Japanese landscape of Gassho-zukuri farmhouses.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go and Timeless Village Life
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Take a chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Takayama.

Hotel Check-out

Hotel Check-in

Today, we recommend exploring popular islands known for their art.

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring. 
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily.

- Explore art installations in preserved homes.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel		
Hotel Check-out

- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!

- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

itinerary.title: Reflecting on Hiroshima's history, then Transfer to Fukuoka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Hiroshima city and Fukuoka at your leisure.

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.
Let's spend more time exploring Hiroshima.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): A UNESCO World Heritage Site representing the impact of war.
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.
- Okonomimura & Hiroshima Station Area: Known for Hiroshima's famous okonomiyaki.

In the afternoon, travel from Hiroshima to Hakata by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

Fukuoka is the gateway to Kyushu. It offers a mix of great food, history, and beautiful coastlines. Try local dishes like tonkotsu ramen, mentaiko, and motsunabe. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>  
- Tenjin/Hakata Night Yatai Hopping: Experience the local street food at yatai stalls. Enjoy options like ramen, yakitori, and oden.

Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Fukuoka.

- Itoshima Area: Explore this resort area with cafes, beaches, and craft shops.
- Munakata Area: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with ancient shrines and museums, where you can enjoy the sea and explore history.

Hotel Check-out

- Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter: A great spot for walking with beautiful streets, cafes, and shops.

- Okayama Castle: Known for its black exterior, it offers stunning views from the tower.
- Korakuen Garden: A beautiful Japanese garden and one of Japan's Three Great Gardens.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Island of Contemporary Art- Naoshima
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we recommend exploring popular islands known for their art.

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring.
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape.
- Explore art installations in preserved homes.
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea.
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>

Breakfast at the Hotel

Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

Enjoy sightseeing in Nagoya!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>

- Noritake Forest: Here, you can learn about the history of ceramics and craftsmanship.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Nagoya to Toba by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

Toba is a port town in Mie Prefecture. It is known for its beautiful sea and island views and for its Ama diving culture.

From Toba, take the shuttle bus to Hachiman Kamado.
Hachiman Kamado is an Ama hut where you can enjoy a meal while Ama divers share stories about their fishing experiences and lives. You will enjoy delicious Ise seafood for lunch!

After lunch, take the shuttle bus back to Toba, then travel from Toba to Kashikojima by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

Around noon, travel from Kashikojima to Toba by limited express train.

itinerary.title: Welcome to Tokyo, Japan
itinerary.description:
Welcome to Japan!
Staff will be waiting for you at Haneda or Narita Airport.
There, you will be given a set of essentials for your trip and will be taken to a taxi stand, limousine bus stop, or train station.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: The adventure kicks off in vibrant Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore Takayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Nagoya by Shinkansen, then take a limited express train to Takayama.

Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Takayama.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takayama Jinya: This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
- Old Town (Sanmachi Street): This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.
- Hida no Sato: This is an open-air museum featuring traditional Gassho style houses. Visitors can experience the original Japanese landscape of Gassho-zukuri farmhouses.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go and Timeless Village Life
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Take a chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: Morning in Takayama and Night life in Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Enjoy a morning in Takayama before departure.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Miyagawa Asaichi: Lively morning market with local specialties and crafts, where you can buy fresh foods.

After that, travel from Takayama to Nagoya by limited express train, then take the Shinkansen to Kyoto.

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Pontocho: Wander this lantern-lit alley by the Kamo River, lined with charming machiya-style restaurants and bars.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let's continue to discover the charm of Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Let's explore beyond Kyoto!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Kyoto?

Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Love gourmet food and shopping? 
Osaka is the place to go. Shop at Osaka's foremost shopping districts Dotonbori and Tsutenkaku Tower and indulge in takoyaki and okonomiyaki until your heart's content!
- Want to see more ancient history? 
Nara is the place to be. Nara predates Kyoto as an ancient capital, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Todaiji Temple, Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and Kofukuji Temple — are just some of many spots with a rich and immersive history.
Nara Park also provides a unique experience where feeding the gentle deer offers a moment to connect with nature.

itinerary.title: Visit Himeji Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and transfer to Okayama
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Fukuoka. You can explore Himeji and Okayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Himeji by Shinkansen.

Himeji is a beautiful castle town with rich history.
Enjoy sightseeing in Himeji!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Himeji Castle: Relish the beauty of Japan’s most famous castle and a UNESCO World Heritage Site!

In the afternoon, travel from Himeji to Okayama by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: A Flexible Day Exploring Kurashiki or Island of Contemporary Art- Naoshima
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we recommend exploring Kurashiki or Naoshima. 

Kurashiki is a historic area with beautiful white-walled buildings.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter: A great spot for walking with beautiful streets, cafes, and shops. 
- Ohara Museum of Art: A top museum with famous artworks, including pieces by Monet. 

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring. 
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape. 
- Explore art installations in preserved homes. 
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea. 
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

itinerary.title: The Land of Sunshine – Okayama and Transfer to Fukuoka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out		

Okayama is rich in history and culture, such as notable castles and gardens.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Okayama Castle: Known for its black exterior, it offers stunning views from the tower.
- Korakuen Garden: A beautiful Japanese garden and one of Japan's Three Great Gardens.

In the afternoon, travel from Okayama to Hakata by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

Fukuoka is the gateway to Kyushu. It offers a mix of great food, history, and beautiful coastlines. Try local dishes like tonkotsu ramen, mentaiko, and motsunabe. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Tenjin/Hakata Night Yatai Hopping: Experience the local street food at yatai stalls. Enjoy options like ramen, yakitori, and oden.

itinerary.title: Let’s enjoy the delicious food and happy flavors of Fukuoka!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel		

Enjoy the sights in Fukuoka. Take the train to explore more of the city.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine: Visit this famous shrine for the god of learning. Walk the traditional path and try the "Ume-ga-e Mochi" rice cakes.
- Ohori Park: Visit this lovely waterfront park in the city center. Stroll around the pond or check out the nearby art museum and the ruins of Fukuoka Castle. 
- Itoshima Area: Explore this resort area with cafes, beaches, and craft shops.
- Munakata Area: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with ancient shrines and museums, where you can enjoy the sea and explore history.
- Yanagawa Area: Take a relaxing boat cruise. Enjoy the boatman's songs while you glide through the scenic countryside and peaceful waterways.

itinerary.title: Reflecting on Hiroshima's history
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel		
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Hiroshima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Hakata to Hiroshima by Shinkansen.

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.
Let's enjoy sightseeing in Hiroshima.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): A UNESCO World Heritage Site representing the impact of war.
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.
- Okonomimura & Hiroshima Station Area: Known for Hiroshima's famous okonomiyaki.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Miyajima & the Sacred Shrine by the Sea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Travel to Miyajima by train and ferry.

Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an ''island of the gods.''
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

itinerary.title: Transfer to and sightseeing in the center of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel		
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Hiroshima to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

Let's spend the afternoon in Tokyo.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.
- Meiji Jingu Shrine: Take a leisurely stroll at the largest shrine in Tokyo!

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?
Here are some great spots to check out.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
The tour ends at hotel check-out.

Thank you for joining our 16-day tour.
We look forward to seeing you again.

itinerary.title: Travel to Nagoya & Castle Town Exploration
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Nagoya and Kashikojima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Nagoya by Shinkansen.

Nagoya is a beautiful city full of samurai history and unique food. 
Enjoy sightseeing in Nagoya!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Nagoya Castle: This is the symbol of Nagoya, known for its golden shachihoko ornaments.
- Noritake Forest: Here, you can learn about the history of ceramics and craftsmanship.
- Osu Shopping District: Explore this lively area, which combines old shops with a youthful vibe.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Toba's Ama diving culture and the delicious seafood
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Nagoya to Toba by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or limited express train.

Toba is a port town in Mie Prefecture. It is known for its beautiful sea and island views and for its Ama diving culture.

From Toba, take the shuttle bus to Hachiman Kamado.  
Hachiman Kamado is an Ama hut where you can enjoy a meal while Ama divers share stories about their fishing experiences and lives. You will enjoy delicious Ise seafood for lunch!

After lunch, take the shuttle bus back to Toba, then travel from Toba to Kashikojima by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in  
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Refined Shima – Pearls, Sea & Culture
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, board the Kashikojima España Cruise, and take in the full beauty of Ago Bay. 

Around noon, travel from Kashikojima to Toba by limited express train.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Mikimoto Pearl Island: This is where the first successful pearl cultivation happened. Here, you can learn about the history of pearl farming. Watch live demonstrations by Ama divers  and shop for beautiful pearl jewelry.

Travel from Toba to Osaka Namba by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or limited express train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: History, Views, and Food in Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Osaka is lively, with busy neighborhoods and a rich food culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Osaka!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

itinerary.title: Day trip to Koyasan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the spiritual center of Shingon Buddhism
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

In the morning, travel from Nankai Naｍba to Gokurakubashi by limited express train, and then transfer to Koyasan by cable car.

Koyasan is a mountain town recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. 
It is surrounded by cedar forests and has deep ties to Japanese Buddhism. Kobo Daishi Kukai practiced asceticism here for over 1,200 years. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Danjo Garan: This is the main area of Koyasan. You can see the famous Konpon Daito Pagoda and Kondo Hall here, which create a beautiful landscape.
- Strolling the Approach: Walk through the calm mountain town, which has souvenir shops and stores that sell Buddhist altar goods.
- Kongobuji Temple: This is the main temple of Koyasan Shingon Buddhism. It features one of Japan’s largest rock gardens, perfect for quiet reflection.

In the evening, return to Nankai Namba by cable car and limited express train.

itinerary.title: Discovering the Timeless Charm of Nara and transfer to Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Nara and Kyoto at your leisure.
In the morning, travel from Osaka to Nara by Sightseeing Limited Express "AONIYOSHI", or limited express train.

Nara is one of Japan's oldest cultural centers, filled with ancient temples, historic shrines, and peaceful parks.
Enjoy sightseeing in Nara!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Todai-ji Temple: The Daibutsuden Hall, home to the Great Buddha, is an impressive sight where you can experience the history and religious culture of Japan.
- Kasuga Taisha Shrine: Characterized by its vermilion-colored structures and more than a thousand stone lanterns. 
- Kofuku-ji Temple: A historic temple featuring a graceful five-story pagoda.
- Nara Park: A vast park blending serene scenery with historic landmarks. Take a moment to interact with and feed the gentle deer that inhabit this unique area.

Transfer to Kyoto by Kintetsu limited express train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Stepping into Kyoto's Timeless Traditions
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this World Heritage temple and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Morning in Kyoto and Night life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kyoto!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A beautiful World Heritage site that is gold-plated.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

In the afternoon, travel from Kyoto to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in
Let's also enjoy the night life in Tokyo.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.

Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?

Here are some great spots to check out:

Enjoy sightseeing in Kanazawa!

In Naoshima
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape.
- Explore art installations in preserved homes.
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea.
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

- Teshima: A calm island with natural beauty and traditional houses. Visit the museum to experience nature through water, sound, and light, and walk the terraced rice fields.
- Inujima: An island focused on art and industrial heritage, featuring the Inujima "Dog Project."
- Ogijima & Megijima: These islands combine daily life with art. You'll find artworks throughout.
- Yashima: A scenic viewpoint in Takamatsu City with a nice path around the Shikoku Mura Museum.

Breakfast at the Hotel		
Hotel Check-out

- Korakuen Garden: A beautiful Japanese garden and one of Japan's Three Great Gardens.

Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an "island of the gods."
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.
- Okonomimura & Hiroshima Station Area: Known for Hiroshima's famous okonomiyaki.

In the afternoon, travel from Hiroshima to Hakata by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

Fukuoka is the gateway to Kyushu. It offers a mix of great food, history, and beautiful coastlines. Try local dishes like tonkotsu ramen, mentaiko, and motsunabe.

Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Fukuoka.

- Itoshima Area: Explore this resort area with cafes, beaches, and craft shops.
- Munakata Area: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with ancient shrines and museums, where you can enjoy the sea and explore history.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Explore Okayama and Kurashiki, the Land of Sunshine
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Hiroshima. You can explore Okayama, Kurashiki and Setouchi Islands at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Okayama by Shinkansen.

Okayama and Kurashiki are rich in history and culture. Kurashiki features charming white-walled streets, while Okayama has notable castles and gardens.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter: A great spot for walking with beautiful streets, cafes, and shops.
- Ohara Museum of Art: A top museum with famous artworks, including pieces by Monet.
- Okayama Castle: Known for its black exterior, it offers stunning views from the tower.
- Korakuen Garden: A beautiful Japanese garden and one of Japan's Three Great Gardens.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Island of Contemporary Art- Naoshima
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we recommend exploring popular islands known for their art.

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring.
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape.
- Explore art installations in preserved homes.
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea.
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

itinerary.title: Reflecting on Hiroshima's history
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Okayama to Hiroshima by Shinkansen.

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.
Enjoy sightseeing in Hiroshima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): A UNESCO World Heritage Site representing the impact of war.
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.
- Okonomimura & Hiroshima Station Area: Known for Hiroshima's famous okonomiyaki.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Miyajima & the Sacred Shrine by the Sea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Travel to Miyajima by train and ferry.

Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an "island of the gods."
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

itinerary.title: Visit Himeji Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore Himeji at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Hiroshima to Himeji by Shinkansen.

Himeji is a beautiful castle town with rich history.
Enjoy sightseeing in Himeji!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Himeji Castle: Admire the beauty of a UNESCO World Heritage Site of Himeji Castle and be sure not to miss the spectacular nighttime illumination.
- Koko-en: This Japanese garden located on the west side of Himeji Castle is a beautifully designed space established on the site of a former Edo-period mansion. Visitors can appreciate the garden’s seasonal landscapes, and matcha tasting is also offered for an authentic cultural experience.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Exploring Kyoto’s Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Himeji to Kyoto by Shinkansen.

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this a UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A beautiful World Heritage site that is gold-plated.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Let's explore beyond Kyoto!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Kyoto?
Here are some great spots to check out.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Love gourmet food and shopping?
Osaka is the place to go. Shop at Osaka's foremost shopping districts Dotonbori and Tsutenkaku Tower and indulge in takoyaki and okonomiyaki until your heart's content!
- Want to see more ancient history?
Nara is the place to be. Nara predates Kyoto as an ancient capital, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Todaiji Temple, Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and Kofukuji Temple — are just some of many spots with a rich and immersive history.
Nara Park also provides a unique experience where feeding the gentle deer offers a moment to connect with nature.

itinerary.title: The Timeless Charm of Kanazawa
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Kanazawa at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Tsuruga by limited express train, then take the Shinkansen to Kanazawa. 

Kanazawa is a city that keeps the feel of an Edo-period castle town while also featuring modern art and architecture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kanazawa!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Higashi Chaya District: Enjoy a magical atmosphere in the evening. It’s a great place for a stroll. 
- Korinbo/Katamachi Area: This lively district is perfect for dining. Try local dishes like seafood and oden.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Kanazawa: Gardens, Arts & Samurai Heritage
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kanazawa.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Omi-cho Market: Visit this market to enjoy local food, especially fresh seafood.
- Kenroku-en Garden: Explore one of Japan's Three Great Gardens, which offers beautiful views in every season.
- Kanazawa Castle Park: This park, next to Kenroku-en, has castle ruins and a large area to walk around.
- 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art: Check out this museum that showcases contemporary art, making it a great stop during your city walk.

Optional chartered taxi tour to Shirakawa-go is available from Kanazawa.
Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, has traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom.

itinerary.title: Morning in Kanazawa and Night life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

In the afternoon, travel from Kanazawa to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

Let's also enjoy the night life in Tokyo.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?
Here are some great spots to check out.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore Nagoya and Kashikojima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Nagoya by Shinkansen.

Nagoya is a beautiful city full of samurai history and unique food.
Enjoy sightseeing in Nagoya!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nagoya Castle: This is the symbol of Nagoya, known for its golden shachihoko ornaments.
- Noritake Forest: Here, you can learn about the history of ceramics and craftsmanship.
- Osu Shopping District: Explore this lively area, which combines old shops with a youthful vibe.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Toba's Ama diving culture and the delicious seafood
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Nagoya to Toba by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

Toba is a port town in Mie Prefecture. It is known for its beautiful sea and island views and for its Ama diving culture.

From Toba, take the shuttle bus to Hachiman Kamado.
Hachiman Kamado is an Ama hut where you can enjoy a meal while Ama divers share stories about their fishing experiences and lives. You will enjoy delicious Ise seafood for lunch!

After lunch, take the shuttle bus back to Toba, then travel from Toba to Kashikojima by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, board the Kashikojima España Cruise, and take in the full beauty of Ago Bay.

Around noon, travel from Kashikojima to Toba by limited express train.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Mikimoto Pearl Island: This is where the first successful pearl cultivation happened. Here, you can learn about the history of pearl farming. Watch live demonstrations by Ama divers and shop for beautiful pearl jewelry.

Travel from Toba to Kyoto by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

Hotel Check-in

- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.
