itinerary.title: Welcome to Tokyo, Japan
itinerary.description:
Welcome to Japan!
Staff will be waiting for you at Haneda or Narita Airport.
There, you will be given a set of essentials for your trip and will be taken to a taxi stand, limousine bus stop, or train station.

Hotel Check-in
itinerary.transportationDetails: Taxi, limousine bus, or train from airport to hotel

itinerary.title: The adventure kicks off in vibrant Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore Takayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Nagoya by Shinkansen, then take a limited express train to Takayama.

Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Takayama.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takayama Jinya: This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
- Old Town (Sanmachi Street): This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.
- Hida no Sato: This is an open-air museum featuring traditional Gassho style houses. Visitors can experience the original Japanese landscape of Gassho-zukuri farmhouses.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go and Timeless Village Life
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Take a chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: Morning in Takayama and Night life in Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Enjoy a morning in Takayama before departure.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Miyagawa Asaichi: Lively morning market with local specialties and crafts, where you can buy fresh foods.

After that, travel from Takayama to Nagoya by limited express train, then take the Shinkansen to Kyoto.

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Pontocho: Wander this lantern-lit alley by the Kamo River, lined with charming machiya-style restaurants and bars.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let's continue to discover the charm of Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Let's explore beyond Kyoto!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Kyoto?

Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Love gourmet food and shopping? 
Osaka is the place to go. Shop at Osaka's foremost shopping districts Dotonbori and Tsutenkaku Tower and indulge in takoyaki and okonomiyaki until your heart's content!
- Want to see more ancient history? 
Nara is the place to be. Nara predates Kyoto as an ancient capital, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Todaiji Temple, Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and Kofukuji Temple — are just some of many spots with a rich and immersive history.
Nara Park also provides a unique experience where feeding the gentle deer offers a moment to connect with nature.

itinerary.title: Visit Himeji Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and transfer to Okayama
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Fukuoka. You can explore Himeji and Okayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Himeji by Shinkansen.

Himeji is a beautiful castle town with rich history.
Enjoy sightseeing in Himeji!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Himeji Castle: Relish the beauty of Japan’s most famous castle and a UNESCO World Heritage Site!

In the afternoon, travel from Himeji to Okayama by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: A Flexible Day Exploring Kurashiki or Island of Contemporary Art- Naoshima
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we recommend exploring Kurashiki or Naoshima. 

Kurashiki is a historic area with beautiful white-walled buildings.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter: A great spot for walking with beautiful streets, cafes, and shops. 
- Ohara Museum of Art: A top museum with famous artworks, including pieces by Monet. 

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring. 
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape. 
- Explore art installations in preserved homes. 
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea. 
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

itinerary.title: The Land of Sunshine – Okayama and Transfer to Fukuoka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out		

Okayama is rich in history and culture, such as notable castles and gardens.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Okayama Castle: Known for its black exterior, it offers stunning views from the tower.
- Korakuen Garden: A beautiful Japanese garden and one of Japan's Three Great Gardens.

In the afternoon, travel from Okayama to Hakata by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

Fukuoka is the gateway to Kyushu. It offers a mix of great food, history, and beautiful coastlines. Try local dishes like tonkotsu ramen, mentaiko, and motsunabe. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Tenjin/Hakata Night Yatai Hopping: Experience the local street food at yatai stalls. Enjoy options like ramen, yakitori, and oden.

itinerary.title: Let’s enjoy the delicious food and happy flavors of Fukuoka!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel		

Enjoy the sights in Fukuoka. Take the train to explore more of the city.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine: Visit this famous shrine for the god of learning. Walk the traditional path and try the "Ume-ga-e Mochi" rice cakes.
- Ohori Park: Visit this lovely waterfront park in the city center. Stroll around the pond or check out the nearby art museum and the ruins of Fukuoka Castle. 
- Itoshima Area: Explore this resort area with cafes, beaches, and craft shops.
- Munakata Area: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with ancient shrines and museums, where you can enjoy the sea and explore history.
- Yanagawa Area: Take a relaxing boat cruise. Enjoy the boatman's songs while you glide through the scenic countryside and peaceful waterways.

itinerary.title: Reflecting on Hiroshima's history
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel		
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Hiroshima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Hakata to Hiroshima by Shinkansen.

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.
Let's enjoy sightseeing in Hiroshima.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): A UNESCO World Heritage Site representing the impact of war.
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.
- Okonomimura & Hiroshima Station Area: Known for Hiroshima's famous okonomiyaki.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Miyajima & the Sacred Shrine by the Sea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Travel to Miyajima by train and ferry.

Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an ''island of the gods.''
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

itinerary.title: Transfer to and sightseeing in the center of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel		
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Hiroshima to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

Let's spend the afternoon in Tokyo.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.
- Meiji Jingu Shrine: Take a leisurely stroll at the largest shrine in Tokyo!

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?
Here are some great spots to check out.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
The tour ends at hotel check-out.

Thank you for joining our 16-day tour.
We look forward to seeing you again.

itinerary.title: Welcome to Japan- Arrival in Hokkaido
itinerary.description:
Welcome to Japan! 
Our staff awaits you at New Chitose Airport with everything needed for your journey. 
Enjoy a comfortable chartered taxi transfer to your hotel for check-in.

itinerary.title: A day exploring Sapporo and the charm of Otaru
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

Spend a full day exploring vibrant Sapporo, renowned for its spacious urban layout, abundant nature, and exceptional Hokkaido cuisine. 

Must-visit attractions include Odori Park, the city's central green space hosting seasonal festivals and offering stunning cityscapes; Susukino, Sapporo's largest entertainment district perfect for experiencing local nightlife and gourmet dining; and the iconic Sapporo Clock Tower, a historic landmark showcasing Hokkaido's pioneering heritage. (*Entrance fees not included)

Consider extending your adventure to picturesque Otaru, a charming historic port town featuring preserved stone warehouses and romantic canals. 
Highlights include the famous Otaru Canal with its nostalgic stone buildings, Kitaichi Glass for exquisite handcrafted glassware, the enchanting Music Box Museum, and Sankaku Market for the freshest seafood experiences.

itinerary.title: Wildlife encounters and scenic wonders in Sounkyo Gorge
itinerary.description:
Enjoy the Hotel breakfast and checkout. 

Travel by chartered taxi to Asahikawa visiting Asahiyama Zoo, Hokkaido's premier wildlife park for observing natural animal behaviors up close. (*Entrance fees not included)

Continue to Sounkyo Gorge in Daisetsuzan National Park, featuring dramatic cliffs, waterfalls, and seasonal landscapes. Witness the contrasting Ginga and Ryusei Falls, Sounkyo's iconic twin waterfalls offering breathtaking scenery. 

Transfer to hotel via chartered taxi for check-in and dinner.

itinerary.title: A scenic journey through peaks, lakes, and open skies
itinerary.description:
Enjoy the Hotel breakfast and checkout.

Take chartered taxi to Kurodake Ropeway, ascending through spectacular gorge and forest views via cable car and chairlift for breathtaking mountain panoramas. (*Entrance fees not included)

Enjoy free lunch in Kitami, then continue to Bihoro Pass, offering stunning overlook views of Lake Kussharo, one of Hokkaido's most iconic scenic spots. 
Explore Japan's largest caldera lake, where vast tranquil waters and surrounding wilderness create serene natural beauty.

Return to hotel via chartered taxi for check-in and dinner.

itinerary.title: Discovering the untamed beauty of Shiretoko and Lake Mashu
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast 

Journey by chartered taxi to Shiretoko, a UNESCO World Heritage site at Hokkaido's northeastern tip, renowned for pristine wilderness, diverse wildlife, and spectacular landscapes.

Key destinations include: Shiretoko Five Lakes, featuring pristine forests, serene lakes, and mountain views accessible via elevated boardwalks; Shiretoko Nature Center for wildlife education and recommended lunch spot; and Shiretoko Pass, one of the "Eight Views of Shiretoko," offering magnificent vistas of Mount Rausu and dramatic mountain scenery.

Return to hotel via chartered taxi for dinner.

itinerary.title: Relaxing moments by the peaceful shores of Lake Akan
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

Enjoy free time exploring Lake Akan area, where rich natural beauty meets indigenous Ainu culture. 
Experience the serene Lake Akan cruise offering stunning views of Mount O-Akan and pristine lakeside scenery. Visit Ainu Kotan village to discover traditional culture, crafts, and performances in authentic shops and theaters. Stroll the Bokke Nature Trail through forests to witness fascinating mud volcanoes created by geothermal activity.(*Entrance fees not included)

Perfect blend of natural wonders and cultural heritage.

Hotel dinner

itinerary.title: Sayonara – Until We Meet Again in Japan!
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast 

The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for spending the last 7 days with our tour.
We hope to see you again!

Begin with delightful city walks through Sapporo and Otaru, then immerse yourself in Ainu cultural sites, volcanic hot spring resorts, and captivating historical theme parks.　Relax by the magnificent shores of Lake Toya, savoring breathtaking lakeside vistas and tranquil moments. Conclude your journey in historic Hakodate, exploring the vibrant morning market and witnessing the spectacular night views from Mount Hakodate.　This thoughtfully balanced itinerary combine urban exploration, natural wonders, and cultural discovery—ideal for first-time visitors to Hokkaido.

This perfectly balanced itinerary combines natural wonders, cultural experiences, and urban exploration for an unforgettable Hokkaido adventure.

itinerary.title: A day exploring Sapporo and the charm of Otaru
itinerary.description:
After a breakfast served at the hotel, spend a full day exploring vibrant Sapporo, renowned for its spacious urban layout, abundant nature, and exceptional Hokkaido cuisine. 

Must-visit attractions include Odori Park, the city's central green space hosting seasonal festivals and offering stunning cityscapes; Susukino, Sapporo's largest entertainment district perfect for experiencing local nightlife and gourmet dining; and the iconic Sapporo Clock Tower, a historic landmark showcasing Hokkaido's pioneering heritage.(*Entrance fees not included)

Consider extending your adventure to picturesque Otaru, a charming historic port town featuring preserved stone warehouses and romantic canals. Highlights include the famous Otaru Canal with its nostalgic stone buildings, Kitaichi Glass for exquisite handcrafted glassware, the enchanting Music Box Museum, and Sankaku Market for the freshest seafood experiences.

itinerary.title: A journey through Ainu culture and volcanic landscapes
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast and checkout.
Send large luggage ahead to Hakodate for hassle-free sightseeing in Lake Toya.　

Full-day chartered taxi tour exploring: UPOPOY National Ainu Museum and Park for immersive cultural experiences with traditional dance and crafts; Noboribetsu Date Jidaimura, an Edo-period theme park featuring ninja performances and samurai atmosphere; dramatic Noboribetsu Hell Valley with volcanic steam vents showcasing Earth's raw power; and Showa-Shinzan Bear Ranch for close encounters with Hokkaido's iconic brown bears. (*Entrance fees not included)
　
Transfer to hotel via chartered taxi for check-in and dinner.

itinerary.title: Relaxing by the tranquil waters of Lake Toya
itinerary.description:
After breakfast at the hotel, enjoy a leisurely day exploring Lake Toya area, Hokkaido's premier caldera lake destination renowned for stunning mountain-lake vistas and rejuvenating hot springs amid pristine natural surroundings. 

Recommended highlights include: Lake Toya cruise offering tranquil views of Nakajima Island and surrounding peaks from the water; Mount Usu Ropeway ascending to panoramic viewpoints overlooking the lake and dramatic volcanic landscape; and Silo Observatory, a popular scenic spot providing breathtaking views of Lake Toya and its central island and complete the day with a Hotel dinner (Entrance fees not included).

itinerary.title: Strolling through Hakodate’s bay district and sparkling night views
itinerary.description:
Breakfast served at the hotel and checkout. Travel by bus to Toya Station, then take a JR Limited Express train to Hakodate Station.
🚃Toya Station → Hakodate Station

Discover Hakodate, southern Hokkaido's charming port city celebrated for stunning ocean vistas, historic streetscapes, and exceptional fresh seafood. 

Must-visit attractions include: Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses, beautifully preserved historical buildings now housing delightful shops and cafes; scenic Bay Area strolls along the harbor showcasing Hakodate's nostalgic maritime charm; Hachiman-zaka slope offering iconic city views stretching toward the sea; and Mount Hakodate's world-renowned night panorama accessible via ropeway, considered among Japan's most spectacular evening vistas. 
(*Entrance fees not included)

Hotel check-in

itinerary.title: The flavors and views of Hakodate at your own pace
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast and continue exploring Hakodate's captivating attractions: 

Hakodate Morning Market - Experience vibrant seafood culture with the freshest catches and authentic Hokkaido delicacies at this bustling marketplace. 
Goryokaku Park - Discover Japan's unique star-shaped fortress ruins offering historical insights and seasonal beauty. 
Ascend Goryokaku Tower for spectacular aerial views of the distinctive pentagonal layout and panoramic city vistas. 
Motomachi District - Stroll charming hillside streets lined with historic churches and elegant Western-style mansions, immersing yourself in Hakodate's rich cultural heritage and architectural treasures from the Meiji era.
(*Entrance fees not included)

itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast at the Hotel.
The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for spending the last 7 days with our tour.
We hope to see you again!

itinerary.title: Sightseeing in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Enjoy sightseeing in Tokyo!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Tokyo Station→ A classic red brick station full of history in the heart of Tokyo.
★Imperial Palace→ The Japanese Royal Family's residence. Wander at your leisure through the Imperial Palace East Garden and Imperial Palace Outer Garden.
★Asakusa→ Don't miss the historic Senso-ji Temple and the bustling Nakamise shopping street
★TOKYO SKYTREE®→ The tallest structure in Japan with stunning sunset views (if timed right). The night view is also excellent. If time permits, a Sumida River cruise is highly recommended. Great views can be enjoyed along both sides of the Sumida River from Asakusa to Odaiba.
★Odaiba→ Don't miss the giant anime robot statue and the vibrant Rainbow Bridge. Ramen Kokugikan and the Takoyaki Museum are also worth considering.

tour.title: Sahoro & Furano Ski Journey
tour.subtitle: Direct Flights to Hokkaido's Powder
tour.description:
This ski tour visits two of Hokkaido’s premier ski resorts: Sahoro Ski Resort and Furano Ski Resort.

itinerary.title: The adventure kicks off in vibrant Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. 
The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Asakusa→This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
★TOKYO SKYTREE®→A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
★The Imperial Palace→A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
★Shibuya Scramble Crossing→A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
★Harajuku→An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together."

itinerary.title: Head to Himeji and explore at your own pace
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

Check out and have your large luggage shipped to Hiroshima, allowing you to explore Himeji with just light luggage. 

Travel from Tokyo to Himeji by Shinkansen in the morning and enjoy a day of sightseeing. 
🚅Tokyo Station→Himeji Station

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
 ★Himeji Castle→A stunning World Cultural Heritage site, known for its beautiful architecture. Climb the steep stairs for a panoramic view of Himeji city. 

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Discover its message of peace in Hiroshima
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast
Take the Shinkansen from Himeji Station to Hiroshima Station then transfer to hotel hotel's shuttle bus servica (30minutes) 
🚅Himeji Station→Hiroshima Station
Once you arrive, you’ll have free time to explore this vibrant city known for its peace and culture.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Atomic Bomb Dome, a World Heritage Site → See with your own eyes the cruelty of war and remember with your heart the wish for peace.
★Hiroshima Prefectural Art Museum → Experience the culture and art of Hiroshima, with a wide variety of artworks on display, including Japanese and Western-style paintings and ceramics.
★Hiroshima Museum of Contemporary Art → Exhibiting mainly contemporary art from Japan and abroad, this museum allows visitors to experience the appeal of new art through creative works and special exhibitions.

When you’re ready to head to the hotel, you can take the free shuttle bus from Hiroshima Station or taxi.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Let’s explore the stunning sights of Miyajima
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast
Enjoy a full day at the "World Heritage site Miyajima"

Travel from Hotel to Miyajima-Island by High-speed Ship (fare included)
★Itsukushima Shrine → A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
★Otorii Gate → Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, "National Treasure Five-story Pagoda", and "National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda" also nearby.
Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple are also in the area and may be of interest. Time permitting, take the Miyajima Ropeway and enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
For those that enjoy history, the Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center are also recommended. The history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima city by ferry and train (afternoon) (using an IC Card Suica)

Free time for sightseeing in Hiroshima city

itinerary.title: Enjoy the sights in Kyoto, just like everyone expects
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast
 Then check out and send your large luggage to Kanazawa. This will help you explore Kyoto more easily.

In the morning, take a shuttle bus or taxi to Hiroshima Station and then board the Shinkansen to Kyoto. 
🚅Hirshima Station→Kyoto Station
Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Kiyomizu-dera Temple → This is one of the most famous temples in Kyoto, where you can enjoy a panoramic view of the city. Watching the sunset here is highly recommended.
★Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka → These are the paths with a Japanese atmosphere; perfect for taking lots of photos!
★Kodaiji Temple → Highly recommend the wonderful bamboo grove.
★Gion → Gion at night is very beautiful; enjoy the restaurants and ryotei on Hanamikoji Street.
★Yasaka Shrine → This historical shrine is also known as one of the best spots for Kyoto’s nightlife.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Wandering through the beautiful sights of Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

Today, let’s take your time to check out some of Kyoto's coolest spots.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Kinkaku-ji Temple→This place is a total gem! It’s a World Heritage site that really sparkles in gold.
★Arashiyama→A super popular spot known for its bamboo groves and the Togetsukyo Bridge. Make sure to try a rickshaw ride while you’re at it!
★Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine→Perfect for photos, this shrine has thousands of those iconic red torii gates stretching out as far as you can see.
★Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi→Great place to dive into some tasty Kyoto food and do a little shopping!"

itinerary.title: Exploring Kanazawa, a city rich in traditions
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast
Then check out and take the Limited Express train or Shinkansen from Kyoto to Kanazawa. 
🚃Kyoto Station→Tsuruga Station
🚅Tsuruga Station→Kanzawa Station

This charming city beautifully combines Edo-period samurai culture with modern art.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Kenroku-en Garden→One of Japan's Three Great Gardens, perfect for a scenic stroll.  
★Kanazawa Castle Park→Explore the grounds of this historic castle.  
★Omicho Market→Enjoy fresh seafood and local treats in this lively market.  

Hotel Check-In

itinerary.title: Samurai Historical Walk Through Kanazawa
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

Explore the beautiful city of Kanazawa, where tradition meets modernity.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Higashi Chaya District→Enjoy the charming old town vibe with cafes and craft shops.
★Nagamachi Samurai District→Discover the picturesque streets of this former samurai neighborhood.
★21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art→A great place to experience contemporary art!

Have fun on your adventure!"

itinerary.title: Check out the enchanting thatched-roof houses in Shirakawa-go
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast
After that, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. This way, you can explore Shirakawa-go and Gero with just a small bag.

In the morning, take a chartered taxi from the hotel to Shirakawa-go. This village is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, known for its gassho-zukuri houses. These traditional homes give you a glimpse into old Japanese life. The village looks different in each season.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Gassho-style Village→Steep thatched roof houses line the streets, and people still live here. 
★Wada House→Visit one of the largest gassho-zukuri houses, which you can tour inside.
★Observation Decks (e.g., Shiroyama)→ These popular spots provide great views of the village and are perfect for photos.

**Shirakawa-go Folk Craft Shops & Cafés**: Discover locally made crafts and taste regional dishes.

After your visit, take hotel's shuttle bus service to the hotel and check in. You’ll have dinner at the hotel."

itinerary.title: Visit Takayama to see its old town and enjoy the hot springs in Gero Onsen
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

In the morning, take a chartered taxi to Takayama. Takayama is a quiet mountain town at the foot of the Northern Alps. You can walk through the streets, try local foods, and shop for crafts.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Old Town→This area has charming streets with wooden buildings. It is home to many local sake breweries and craft shops.  
★Takayama Jinya→Visit this historic site, which was once an Edo-period government office with preserved wooden structures.

After that, take a chartered taxi to Takayama Station. From there, board the Limited Express train to Gero.
🚃Takayama Station→Gero Station

While in Gero, you may want to explore the hot spring town.

Check-in After checking in, enjoy dinner at the hotel

itinerary.title: Fun visit to Inuyama Castle, and heading back to Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

Take hotel's shuttle bus service from hotel to Gero Station.
Take the Limited Express train to Mino-Ota then transfer to Inuyama, a historic castle town along the Kiso River.
🚃Gero Station→Inuyama-yuen Station

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>  *Entrance fees not included
★Inuyama Castle→Home to Japan's oldest wooden tower, this National Treasure offers a glimpse of the Warring States period and great views from the top floor.

Travel to Nagoya by Limited Express train, then take the Shinkansen to Tokyo.
🚃Inuyama Station→Meitetsu Nagoya Station
🚅Nagoya Station→Tokyo Station

Hotel Check-in

Enjoy evening sightseeing in Tokyo.  
★Nihonbashi/Ginza→A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo? Here are some great spots to check out:

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Kamakura→A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
★Nikko→Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
★Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi→Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.

Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
Hotel breakfast
 After check-out, the tour ends. 
Thank you for spending the last 14 days with our tour. We hope to see you again!

tour.title: From Sacred Mountains to Coastal Calm
tour.subtitle: Faith & Tradition: Koyasan, Ise-Shima & Shirakawa-go Hotel Standard: Departures from April to November
tour.description:
The journey begins with Tokyo's vibrant cityscape. Then it continues to Kashikojima, a coastal area surrounded by the sea, where you can experience the gentle nature of Ise-Shima and savor fresh seafood.
In Kyoto and Nara, you will visit temples and shrines steeped in a thousand years of history, allowing you to experience a moment of connection with Japan's spiritual culture.
The highlight of the journey is Koyasan. Surrounded by lush green mountains, this sacred site offers a space filled with silence and prayer, where you can slowly calm your mind. Staying at the hotel and enjoying vegetarian cuisine, you will experience a time unlike your daily life.
Afterwards, you will enjoy the bustling atmosphere of Osaka and the traditional townscape of Takayama, and the journey will return to a rhythm that harmonizes with nature and human life. The balance of stillness and movement that lingers in your heart is the essence of this journey.

itinerary.title: Welcome to Japan- Arrival in Tokyo

Welcome to Japan!
Staff will be waiting for you at Haneda or Narita Airport.
There, you will be given a set of essentials for your trip and will be taken to a taxi stand, limousine bus stop, or train station.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: The adventure kicks off in vibrant Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Visiting Ise, the Spiritual Heart of Japan
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore  Kashikojima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Nagoya by Shinkansen, then take the limited express train and the local bus to Ise Jingu Shrine.

Ise Jingu shrine is Japan's most famous shrine with about 2,000 years of history. It is a peaceful place where you can reflect as you walk along the tree-lined path.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Naiku (Inner Shrine): This is the main part of Ise Grand Shrine, where Amaterasu Omikami is honored. You will see beautiful sights like Uji Bridge and the Isuzu River.
- Okage Yokocho: This street has buildings from the Edo and Meiji periods. You can try local dishes like Ise udon and Akafuku mochi.

After visiting Ise Jingu Shrine, take the reserved shuttle bus from Ise Jingu Shrine to your hotel.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Refined Shima – Pearls, Sea & Culture and transfer to Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, board the Kashikojima España Cruise, and take in the full beauty of Ago Bay.

After that, take the limited express train from Kashkojima to Toba.
Toba is a port town in Mie Prefecture. It is known for its beautiful sea and island views and for its ama diving culture.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Mikimoto Pearl Island: This is where the first successful pearl cultivation happened. Here, you can learn about the history of pearl farming. Watch live demonstrations by Ama divers and shop for beautiful pearl jewelry.

In the afternoon, travel from Toba to Kyoto by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Exploring Kyoto’s Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Nara's Sacred Heritage
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Nara and Koyasan at your leisure.
In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Kintetsu Nara by limited express train.

Nara is one of Japan's oldest cultural centers, filled with ancient temples, historic shrines, and peaceful parks.
Enjoy sightseeing in Nara.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Todai-ji Temple: The Daibutsuden Hall, home to the Great Buddha, is an impressive sight where you can experience the history and religious culture of Japan.
- Nara Park: A vast park blending serene scenery with historic landmarks. Take a moment to interact with and feed the gentle deer that inhabit this unique area.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Sacred Mountain Retreat – Koyasan
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Kintetsu Nara to Osaka Namba by Shinkansen, then take the local train from Shin-Osaka to Namba. Then, transfer to Nankai Namba and travel from Nankai Naｍba to Gokurakubashi by limited express train, and then transfer to Koyasan by cable car.

Koyasan is a mountain town recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
It is surrounded by cedar forests and has deep ties to Japanese Buddhism. Kobo Daishi Kukai practiced asceticism here for over 1,200 years.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Danjo Garan: This is the main area of Koyasan. You can see the famous Konpon Daito Pagoda and Kondo Hall here, which create a beautiful landscape.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: A Peaceful Stroll Through Koyasan
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, let's wander slowly through the sacred grounds of Koyasan.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Strolling the Approach: Walk through the calm mountain town, which has souvenir shops and stores that sell Buddhist altar goods.
- Kongobuji Temple: This is the main temple of Koyasan Shingon Buddhism. It features one of Japan’s largest rock gardens, perfect for quiet reflection.

In the afternoon, travel from Koyasan to Gokurakubashi by cable car, then take the limited express train to Nankai Namba. 

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: History, Views, and Food in Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Osaka is lively, with busy neighborhoods and a rich food culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Osaka!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Takayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Namba to Shin-Osaka by local train, then take the Shinkansen to Nagoya. Then, transfer to Takayama by limited express train.

Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.

Enjoy sightseeing in Takayama.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takayama Jinya: This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
- Old Town (Sanmachi Street): This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.
- Hida no Sato: This is an open-air museum featuring traditional Gassho style houses. Visitors can experience the original Japanese landscape of Gassho-zukuri farmhouses.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go: Thatched Roof Villages
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

Take a chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: Morning in Takayama and Night life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Enjoy a morning in Takayama before departure.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Miyagawa Asaichi: Lively morning market with local specialties and crafts, where you can buy fresh foods.

After that, travel from Takayama to Nagoya by limited express train, then take the Shinkansen to Tokyo.

Hotel Check-in

Let's also enjoy the night life in Tokyo.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?
Here are some great spots to check out.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

tour.title: A Journey of Culture, Peace, and Spiritual Reflection
tour.subtitle: Faith & Tradition: Koyasan,Miyajima & Shirakawa-go Hotel Standard: Departures from April to November
tour.description:
Beginning with the modern glamour of Tokyo, you will experience a quiet sense of emotion as you encounter prayers for peace in Hiroshima.
After experiencing the lively food culture and warm hospitality of Osaka, you will head to Koyasan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, nestled deep in the mountains.
At Koyasan, you will encounter solemn temples and moss-covered Okunoin, where you can find peace of mind. In this sacred space, far removed from everyday life, you can immerse yourself in the "time of prayer" that the Japanese people have cherished.
As the journey continues to Kyoto and Takayama, you will experience the beauty of Japan's traditions and the wisdom of living in harmony with nature, further deepening the tranquility of the trip.
This is a journey that blends modernity and tradition, bustling energy and tranquility, leaving a lasting sense of peace in your heart.

Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.
Enjoy sightseeing in Hiroshima!

tour.description:
After kicking off your journey in Tokyo, head away from the hustle and bustle to Koyasan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a sacred place in Japanese Buddhism.
In this place where Kukai's prayers from 1,200 years ago still linger, you can enjoy a relaxing experience through the solemn temple complex, the mystical atmosphere of the sacred site Okunoin, and a stay at a temple lodging.
In Kyoto, you can enjoy the beauty and delicacy of Japanese culture in the cityscape. In Takayama, you can experience the traditional wooden houses and simple mountain life, adding a gentle afterglow to your journey.  
This route, which emphasizes feeling rather than superficial sightseeing, is a luxurious journey that allows you to confront yourself. In the stillness, a deep sense of satisfaction resides.

tour.description:
The journey begins with Tokyo's vibrant cityscape. Then it continues to Kashikojima, a coastal area surrounded by the sea, where you can experience the gentle nature of Ise-Shima and savor fresh seafood.
In Kyoto and Nara, you will visit temples and shrines steeped in a thousand years of history, allowing you to experience a moment of connection with Japan's spiritual culture.
The highlight of the journey is Koyasan. Surrounded by lush green mountains, this sacred site offers a space filled with silence and prayer, where you can slowly calm your mind. Staying at the hotel and enjoying vegetarian cuisine, you will experience a time unlike your daily life.
Afterwards, you will enjoy the bustling atmosphere of Osaka and the traditional townscape of Takayama, and the journey will return to a rhythm that harmonizes with nature and human life. The balance of stillness and movement that lingers in your heart is the essence of this journey.

tour.description: Beginning with the modern glamour of Tokyo, you will experience a quiet sense of emotion as you encounter prayers for peace in Hiroshima. After experiencing the lively food culture and warm hospitality of Osaka, you will head to Koyasan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, nestled deep in the mountains. At Koyasan, you will encounter solemn temples and moss-covered Okunoin, where you can find peace of mind. In this sacred space, far removed from everyday life, you can immerse yourself in the "time of prayer" that the Japanese people have cherished. As the journey continues to Kyoto and Takayama, you will experience the beauty of Japan's traditions and the wisdom of living in harmony with nature, further deepening the tranquility of the trip. This is a journey that blends modernity and tradition, bustling energy and tranquility, leaving a lasting sense of peace in your heart.

itinerary.title: The adventure kicks off in vibrant Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Visit Himeji Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Himeji and Hiroshima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Himeji by Shinkansen.

Himeji is a beautiful castle town with rich history.
Enjoy sightseeing in Himeji!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Himeji Castle: Admire the beauty of a UNESCO World Heritage Site of Himeji Castle and be sure not to miss the spectacular nighttime illumination.
- Koko-en: This Japanese garden located on the west side of Himeji Castle is a beautifully designed space established on the site of a former Edo-period mansion. Visitors can appreciate the garden’s seasonal landscapes, and matcha tasting is also offered for an authentic cultural experience.

In the afternoon, travel from Himeji to Hiroshima by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Miyajima & the Sacred Shrine by the Sea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Travel to Miyajima by train and ferry.

Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an "island of the gods."
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

itinerary.title: Reflecting on Hiroshima's history
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Hiroshima to Shin-Osaka by Shinkansen.

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.
Enjoy sightseeing in Hiroshima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): A UNESCO World Heritage Site representing the impact of war.
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.
- Okonomimura & Hiroshima Station Area: Known for Hiroshima's famous okonomiyaki.

In the afternoon, travel from Hiroshima to Shin-Osaka by Shinkansen.
Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: History, Views, and Food in Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Osaka is lively, with busy neighborhoods and a rich food culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Osaka!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

itinerary.title: Sacred Mountain Retreat – Koyasan
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore Koyasan at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Shin-Osaka to Namba by local train, then take the limited express train from Nankai Namba to Gokurakubashi. Then, transfer to Koyasan by cable car.

Koyasan is a mountain town recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
It is surrounded by cedar forests and has deep ties to Japanese Buddhism. Kobo Daishi Kukai practiced asceticism here for over 1,200 years.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Danjo Garan: This is the main area of Koyasan. You can see the famous Konpon Daito Pagoda and Kondo Hall here, which create a beautiful landscape.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: A Peaceful Stroll Through Koyasan
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, let's wander slowly through the sacred grounds of Koyasan.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Strolling the Approach: Walk through the calm mountain town, which has souvenir shops and stores that sell Buddhist altar goods.
- Kongobuji Temple: This is the main temple of Koyasan Shingon Buddhism. It features one of Japan’s largest rock gardens, perfect for quiet reflection.

In the afternoon, travel from Koyasan to Gokurakubashi by cable car, then take the limited express train to Shin-Imamiya. Then, transfer to Kyoto by local train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Exploring Kyoto’s Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Takayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Nagoya by Shinkansen, then take the limited express to Takayama.

Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.

Enjoy sightseeing in Takayama.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takayama Jinya: This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
- Old Town (Sanmachi Street): This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.
- Hida no Sato: This is an open-air museum featuring traditional Gassho style houses. Visitors can experience the original Japanese landscape of Gassho-zukuri farmhouses.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go: Thatched Roof Villages
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

Take a chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: Morning in Takayama and Night life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Enjoy a morning in Takayama before departure.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Miyagawa Asaichi: Lively morning market with local specialties and crafts, where you can buy fresh foods.

After that, travel from Takayama to Nagoya by limited express train, then take the Shinkansen to Tokyo.

Hotel Check-in

Let's also enjoy the night life in Tokyo.
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?
Here are some great spots to check out.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for joining the 15-day tour!
We look forward to seeing you again.

itinerary.title: Cherry Blossom Trails of Nara by Kintetsu Railway
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel 

Today, let’s head out to enjoy the beautiful cherry blossoms of Nara.

Travel by Kintetsu train to Haibara, then continue by bus to Takami-no-Sato, a spectacular mountain garden surrounded by over 1,000 weeping cherry trees. During the spring bloom, the slopes are transformed into a sea of pink, with panoramic views of the surrounding mountains from the garden’s viewpoints.

After enjoying the blossoms, return to Haibara and continue by Kintetsu Railway to Hasedera Temple. Known as the “Temple of Flowers,” Hasedera is a historic Buddhist temple surrounded by nature, with a beautiful temple complex built into the mountainside. Its long stairway, wooden Main Hall and seasonal flowers create a particularly atmospheric setting in spring.

Return to Osaka by Kintetsu train.

<Optional Bus Tour Available>
For an easier way to see Nara’s highlights, we recommend the Perfect Nara Park Tour, an English-guided sightseeing bus operated by Nara Kotsu. The tour visits Todaiji, Kasuga Taisha and Mount Wakakusa with a professional English-speaking guide.

Return to Osaka by Kintetsu train.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Fukuoka is the gateway to Kyushu, a city known for its food, history, and seaside views. Try local dishes like tonkotsu ramen, mentaiko, and motsunabe.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Yanagawa Boat Cruise → Enjoy a relaxing boat ride in Yanagawa, the “Water Capital,” with lovely countryside views and singing boatmen.
★Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine → Visit this famous shrine for the god of learning. Walk the traditional path and try the “Ume-ga-e Mochi” rice cakes.
★Itoshima Area → Explore this resort area with cafes, beaches, and craft shops.
★Tenjin / Hakata Night Yatai Hopping → Taste local favorites at night food stalls, including ramen, yakitori, and oden.

itinerary.title: The City of Light and Blessing, Nagasaki
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kumamoto. This allows you to explore Nagasaki without heavy bags.

In the morning, take the limited express train and Shinkansen from Hakata Station to Nagasaki Station. 
🚃Hakata Station→Takeo Onsen Station
🚅Takeo Onsen Station→Nagasaki Station
The city has a rich trade history and blends foreign and Japanese cultures.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Nagasaki Atomic Bomb Museum → Learn about Nagasaki's history and view peace-promoting exhibits.
★Peace Park → A tranquil park with the Peace Statue, symbolizing prayers for peace worldwide.
★Urakami Cathedral → Nagasaki's main Catholic church, rebuilt after the bombing.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Gunkanjima: A depiction of a city's collapse
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

In the morning, head to Nagasaki Port.
★Gunkanjima (Battleship Island) → Gunkanjima is an uninhabited island that was once a busy coal mine, known for its fortress-like appearance. The cruise lets you see the ruins and learn about Nagasaki’s industrial history.

After the cruise, enjoy more of Nagasaki.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Dejima → This was Japan’s only connection to the outside world during the Edo period, featuring restored buildings from that time.
★Glover Garden → Enjoy beautiful views of the port and Western-style buildings on a hill.
★Oura Cathedral → Japan’s oldest Christian church, a World Heritage Site with a striking white exterior and stained glass.
★Megane Bridge → The oldest stone arch bridge in Japan; its reflection looks like a pair of glasses.
★Sofuku-ji Temple → The oldest surviving building in Nagasaki City, built in the 1600s.

itinerary.title: Where? Higo, Kumamoto!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel Check out.

In the morning, take the Shinkansen and JR limited express train from Nagasaki to Kumamoto. 
🚅Nagasaki Station→Takeo Onsen Station
🚃Takeo Onsen Station→Shin Tosu Station
🚅Shin Tosu Station→Kumamoto Station
Kumamoto is known for its natural beauty and historic castle town.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Kumamoto Castle → One of Japan's Three Great Castles, featuring impressive stone walls and a rebuilt main keep. Check out the nighttime illumination.

Hotel check-in

itinerary.title: Explore Kumamoto with all five senses.
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel Check-out

Take a chartered taxi to Kumamoto and Takachiho

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Suizenji Jojuen Garden → Walk through this beautiful Japanese garden with ponds and lawns.
★Aso-Kuju National Park
Kusasenri → Visit this scenic area with views of Aso's wide grasslands and surrounding mountains.
Nakadake Crater → See the famous crater that emits smoke up close (access may depend on the weather).
★Takachiho Amaterasu Railway → Enjoy a ride on open-air sightseeing cars through the gorge with great views.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Welcome to Takachiho, a place known for its myths.
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel Check-Out

Take a chartered  taxi to Takachiho
Takachiho is a mountainous area famous for its connection to Japanese mythology. It has beautiful valleys, waterfalls, and shrines.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Takachiho Gorge → This valley features cliffs created by volcanic activity. We suggest booking a boat trip in advance to see Manai Falls up close.
★Amanoiwato Shrine → This shrine is linked to the sun goddess Amaterasu Omikami and is located in the mountains, giving it a mysterious feel.

Transfer to Beppu by chartered taxi

Hotel check-in and enjoy dinner at the hotel

itinerary.title: A century of gratitude will be felt in tomorrow's hot springs.
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

Beppu is one of Japan's top hot spring destinations.
It is known for its steam-filled scenery.
A popular tour here is the ""Hell Tour,"" which shows visitors interesting natural sites like red hot springs and blue steam pools.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>*Entrance fees not included
★Sea Hell→This is Beppu's most famous site, featuring bright blue boiling water.
★Blood Pond Hell→This spot has striking red hot spring water and is considered Japan's oldest hell.
★Whirlpool Hell→Here, a geyser erupts at regular intervals.
★White Pond Hell→This is a peaceful place with large, milky-white hot spring water.
★Oniyama Hell→At this unique location, you can see crocodiles warmed by natural heat.

Also, don’t miss the chance to try hot spring eggs and foot baths at different places around Beppu.

Dinner at the hotel

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Let’s enjoy the delicious food and happy flavors of Fukuoka!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Fukuoka is the gateway to Kyushu, a city known for its food, history, and seaside views. 
Try local dishes like tonkotsu ramen, mentaiko, and motsunabe.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Yanagawa Boat Cruise→Enjoy a relaxing boat ride in Yanagawa, the ""Water Capital,"" with lovely countryside views and singing boatmen.
★Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine→Visit this famous shrine for the god of learning. Walk the traditional path and try the ""Ume-ga-e Mochi"" rice cakes.
★Itoshima Area→Explore this resort area with cafes, beaches, and craft shops.
★Tenjin/Hakata Night Yatai Hopping→Taste local favorites at night food stalls, including ramen, yakitori, and oden.

itinerary.title: Treasure Chest of Southern Kyushu: Kagoshima
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel  
Have breakfast at the hotel and check out. Ship your large luggage to Kumamoto so you can explore Kagoshima easily.

In the morning, take the Shinkansen from Hakata Station to Kagoshima Chuo Station. 
🚅Hakata Station→Kagoshima Chuo Station
Kagoshima offers great views of Sakurajima and a relaxed seaside atmosphere.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Sengan-en Garden→ This garden has beautiful scenery and rich history with views of Sakurajima.  
★Satsuma Kiriko Glassware Shops→Try making your own glass pieces and enjoy local treats like Shirokuma, a milk-flavored shaved ice, and matcha.  
★Bastica Yatai Village→Visit various izakayas to enjoy local dishes and Kurobuta berkshire pork.  

Hotel Check-in
After sightseeing, return to check in at your hotel.

itinerary.title: Discover Satsuma's Little Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel  
After checking out, explore southern Kagoshima by chartered Taxi.

★Chiran Samurai Residences→ Known as ""Satsuma's Little Kyoto,"" this area features charming streets with stone walls and hedges, preserving samurai culture in a peaceful setting.
★Lake Ikeda:→As Kyushu's largest lake, it offers stunning views of Mount Kaimon.
★Mount Kaimon→Often called ""Satsuma's Fuji,"" this conical mountain provides beautiful scenic views.
★Nagasakibana→This cape offers great views of Mount Kaimon across the sea, making it a popular photo spot.

Hotel Check-in

We recommend trying the sand bath at the hotel. Here, you lie in sand heated by hot springs, promoting relaxation and detoxification.

Dinner at the hotel

Check out.

Try the exclusive sweets from Tamatebako in its cute, retro interior. After that, take the Shinkansen to Kumamoto. 
🚅Kagoshima Chuo Station→Kumamoto Station
Kumamoto is known for its natural beauty and historic castle town.

Hotel check-in

itinerary.title: Explore Kumamoto with all five senses.
itinerary.description:

Check-out

Chartered Taxi Tour of Kumamoto
★Suizenji Jojuen Garden→Walk through this beautiful Japanese garden with ponds and lawns.  
★Aso-Kuju National Park
★Kusasenri→Visit this scenic area with views of Aso's wide grasslands and surrounding mountains.

Hotel Check-in  Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Welcome to Takachiho, a place known for its myths.
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel 

Check-Out

Chartered Taxi Tour of Takachiho  
Takachiho is a mountainous area famous for its connection to Japanese mythology. It has beautiful valleys, waterfalls, and shrines.  

★Takachiho Gorge→This valley features cliffs created by volcanic activity. We suggest booking a boat trip in advance to see Manai Falls up close.  
★Amanoiwato Shrine→This shrine is linked to the sun goddess Amaterasu Omikami and is located in the mountains, giving it a mysterious feel.  

Transfer to Beppu by chartered Taxi  

Check-In Dinner at the hotel

itinerary.title: A century of gratitude will be felt in tomorrow's hot springs.
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

Beppu is one of Japan's top hot spring destinations. 
It is known for its steam-filled scenery. 
A popular tour here is the ""Hell Tour,"" which shows visitors interesting natural sites like red hot springs and blue steam pools.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Sea Hell→This is Beppu's most famous site, featuring bright blue boiling water.
★Blood Pond Hell→This spot has striking red hot spring water and is considered Japan's oldest hell.
★Whirlpool Hell→Here, a geyser erupts at regular intervals.
★White Pond Hell→This is a peaceful place with large, milky-white hot spring water.
★Oniyama Hell→At this unique location, you can see crocodiles warmed by natural heat.

Also, don’t miss the chance to try hot spring eggs and foot baths at different places around Beppu.

Dinner at the hotel

itinerary.description:

Unzen-Amakusa National Park

Kusasenri→Visit this scenic area with views of Aso's wide grasslands and surrounding mountains.  

Hotel Check in  Dinner at the hotel

itinerary.title: A century of gratitude will be felt in tomorrow's hot springs.
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

Beppu is one of Japan's top hot spring destinations. It is known for its steam-filled scenery. A popular tour here is the ""Hell Tour,"" which shows visitors interesting natural sites like red hot springs and blue steam pools.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Sea Hell→This is Beppu's most famous site, featuring bright blue boiling water.
★Blood Pond Hell→This spot has striking red hot spring water and is considered Japan's oldest hell.
★Whirlpool Hell→Here, a geyser erupts at regular intervals.
★White Pond Hell→This is a peaceful place with large, milky-white hot spring water.
★Oniyama Hell→At this unique location, you can see crocodiles warmed by natural heat.

Also, don’t miss the chance to try hot spring eggs and foot baths at different places around Beppu.

Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Cities where people and nature coexist
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel Check out from the hotel
  
Full-Day Tour from the hotel by Chartered Taxi  

Explore the natural beauty of Yufuin and the historical charm of Hita in one day.

<Yufuin>  
★Kinrin Lake→Enjoy lakeside walks, especially beautiful in the morning mist.  
★Yunotsubo Street→This popular walking area has many sweet shops, stores, and galleries.  
★Mt. Yufu Viewpoint→Take photos with the stunning Mt. Yufu in the background.  
★Yufuin Floral Village→A cute town that looks like a scene from a picture book.

<Hita>
★Hita Mameda-machi→This historic area has streets with white-walled buildings. It’s great for walking, with many shops and cafes.  
★Hita Yakisoba→Try this local dish of crispy, savory noodles and crunchy bean sprouts.

Check in to the hotel Dinner at the hotel

itinerary.title: Discover the Land of Tea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel Check out of the hotel. 

Morning Tour of Yame by Chartered Taxi
Experience the rich flavor and aroma of tea while learning about traditional tea culture in Yame, a top tea-producing area in Japan.  

Afternoon: Free Time in Fukuoka
Fukuoka is the gateway to Kyushu. It offers a mix of great food, history, and beautiful coastlines. Try local dishes like tonkotsu ramen, mentaiko, and motsunabe. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
★Ohori Park→Visit this lovely waterfront park in the city center. Stroll around the pond or check out the nearby art museum and the ruins of Fukuoka Castle. 
★Tenjin/Hakata Night Yatai Hopping→Experience the local street food at yatai stalls. Enjoy options like ramen, yakitori, and oden. 

Check-in at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Let’s enjoy the delicious food and happy flavors of Fukuoka!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Enjoy the sights in Fukuoka. Take the train to explore more of the city.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine→Visit this famous shrine for the god of learning. Walk the traditional path and try the ""Ume-ga-e Mochi"" rice cakes.
★Itoshima Area→Explore this resort area with cafes, beaches, and craft shops.
★Munakata Area→A peaceful World Heritage site with ancient shrines and museums, where you can enjoy the sea and explore history."

Hotel Check-in
This luxury hotel opened in 1890 and is a well-known symbol of Japan.

itinerary.title: Tradition and Modern Life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Matsusaka Beef & Shima Luxury Escape
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kyoto. You can explore Ise-Shima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Nagoya by Shinkansen.
Then, transfer to Matsuzaka by limited express train.

Have lunch at Wadakin, a famous restaurant known for Matsusaka beef, a top-quality wagyu enjoyed in Japan and around the world.

After lunch, travel from Matsuzaka to Kashikojima by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in
Today's Hotel is the Shima Kanko Hotel The Bay Suites. This luxury resort overlooks Ago Bay and has only suite accommodations. It hosted the G7 Ise-Shima Summit and is a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World.

Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Refined Shima – Pearls, Sea & Culture
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, explore the Ise-Shima area. This resort is known for its beautiful Rias coastline and maritime culture.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Kashikojima Espana Cruise: Take a cruise around Ago Bay to see the stunning archipelago from the water.
- Ama Hut Experience: Discover traditional ama diving techniques and taste local seafood like spiny lobster and abalone. Make a reservation for this experience.
- Mikimoto Pearl Island: This is where the first successful pearl cultivation happened. Here, you can learn about the history of pearl farming. Watch live demonstrations by Ama divers and shop for beautiful pearl jewelry.

Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Sacred Ise & Luxury Ride to Kyoto
Exploring Kyoto’s Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this World Heritage temple and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we will take a longer trip to explore Kyoto’s famous sights.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Kanazawa Old Town & Stylish Districts
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel 
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Kanazawa at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Tsuruga by limited express train, then transfer to Kanazawa by Shinkansen.

Kanazawa is a city that keeps the feel of an Edo-period castle town while also featuring modern art and architecture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kanazawa!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Higashi Chaya District: Enjoy a magical atmosphere. It’s a great place for a stroll.
- Korinbo/Katamachi Area: This lively district is perfect for dining. Try local dishes like seafood and oden.

Hotel Check-in
Today's Hotel is THE HOTEL SANRAKU KANAZAWA. This hotel offers a great cultural experience, showing off Kanazawa's traditional crafts and design.

itinerary.title: Kanazawa Culture & Art Day
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Explore more of Kanazawa!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Omi-cho Market: Visit this market to enjoy local food, especially fresh seafood.
- Kenroku-en Garden: Explore one of Japan's Three Great Gardens, which offers beautiful views in every season.
- Kanazawa Castle Park: This park, next to Kenroku-en, has castle ruins and a large area to walk around.
- 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art: Check out this museum that showcases contemporary art, making it a great stop during your city walk.

Optional chartered taxi tour to Shirakawa-go is available from Kanazawa.
Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, has traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom.

itinerary.title: Refined Tokyo Revisited
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Kanazawa to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- The National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo: This museum shows many important pieces of Japanese art from modern to contemporary times.
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.
- Kabuki-za: This theater is famous for Kabuki performances, which are Japan's traditional theater. You can also see just one act if you prefer.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?

 Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Farewell – Until Your Next Journey
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
The tour ends at hotel check-out.

Please take the airport shuttle taxi. Thank you for spending the last 12 days with our tour. 
We hope to see you again!

tour.subtitle: A Premium Journey Through Shiga's Hidden Gems
tour.description: Enjoy a premium journey across Japan, combining seamless Shinkansen travel with private sightseeing taxis for a comfortable and refined experience. Stay at high-end hotels, travel in the spacious comfort of Green Car (the first-class carriages on Japan's trains), and explore each destination with the ease of a dedicated vehicle. This tour takes you beyond the usual routes to discover some of Japan's lesser-known yet remarkable destinations. Visit Hikone Castle, a designated national treasure, stroll through the historic merchant town of Omihachiman, enjoy a cruise on Lake Biwa, and experience the serene moss gardens of Sanzen-in Temple in Ohara, Kyoto. Alongside these hidden gems, you will also have plenty of time to explore Japan's iconic cities, including Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka. This carefully designed route offers the perfect balance of cultural heritage, natural beauty, and vibrant city life — bringing together the best of both traditional and modern Japan in one unforgettable journey.

itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Take a chartered taxi for sightseeing.

In the morning, board the Biwako Cruise Michigan.

Let's continue your journey through Shiga.

Hotel Check-out
