Head to the hotel by chartered taxi.

Let's spend more time exploring Hiroshima.

Travel to Miyajima by ferry.
Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an "island of the gods."
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry.

tour.title: Alpine Wonders of Central Japan
tour.subtitle: Alpine Peaks Meet Ancient Streets: Departures from June to October
tour.description:
This nature route takes you through the beautiful landscapes of central Japan, including Mount Fuji, the Japanese Alps, lakes, and highlands. 
You will start in Tokyo and see changing scenery every day. You'll explore the foothills of Mount Fuji, the highlands of Shinshu, and the clear streams of Kamikochi. You will also visit the mountain villages of Hida Takayama and Shirakawa-go. 
The journey includes stays at hot spring resorts and mountain hotels, allowing you to enjoy both nature and culture at a comfortable pace. 
In the later part of the trip, you'll cross the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, known for its amazing mountain views. This loop combines natural beauty with comfort, helping you experience the true essence of Japan's land.
tour.shortDescription: 12-day alpine tour (June–Oct): Mt Fuji, Kamikochi hiking, Shirakawa-go, and Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route through Japan's mountainous heartland.
highlights: Lake Kawaguchi offers beautiful views of Mount Fuji and the Arakura Fuji Sengen Shrine.

In Chubu Sangaku National Park, you can explore the clear streams and mountain landscapes of Kamikochi.
Visit Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with traditional Gassho-zukuri farmhouses
Experience the stunning mountains by taking the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route.

itinerary.title: Kamikochi: The Heart of the Japanese Alps

itinerary.description:

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take the chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: From Mountain Towns to the Sea of Japan
The Legendary Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After check out, travel from Dentetsu Toyama to Tateyama. 

This trip takes us through Chubu Sangaku National Park. The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route connects Toyama and Nagano Prefectures. It is Japan's main mountain route. You can enjoy the beautiful Northern Alps by using different types of transportation, such as ropeways, cable cars, and buses.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Murodo: This is the highest point on the Alpine Route, at about 2,450 meters. Here, you can see alpine plants and volcanic land.
- Mikurigaike Pond: This is a volcanic lake in the Murodo area. On clear days, you can see the mountains reflecting on the lake's surface.
- Daikanbo: You can reach this viewpoint by ropeway. It offers a great view of the Tateyama mountain range.
- Kurobe Dam: This is one of Japan's largest arch dams. Visitors can walk across the dam.

After sightseeing, take the chertered taxi to Yudanaka Onsen. 

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Meet Japan’s Wild Monkeys in Nagano
itinerary.description:

Jigokudani Monkey Park is a special place where you can see wild Japanese macaques. The park also has nature trails where you can enjoy seasonal plants, streams, and the forest's beauty. This makes it a great spot to connect with both wildlife and nature.

After your visit, take the limited express train from Yudanaka to Nagano.

You have two sightseeing options: Plan A and Plan B.
[Plan A]  
When you arrive at Nagano, enjoy lunch before taking the Shinkansen. 
[Plan B]  
Enjoy approximately two hours of free time to explore Zenko-ji Temple.  
Zenko-ji Temple is a historic Buddhist temple dating back over 1,400 years. 

In the afternoon, travel from Nagano to Tokyo by limited express train, then transfer to Shinjuku by local train.

tour.description:
This itinerary offers a nice mix of nature and culture. It takes you through the beautiful Japanese Alps and into historic cities in the Hokuriku and Kansai regions.
You will start in Tokyo and travel through Nagano. Then, you will cross the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route and enjoy the stunning mountain views and fresh air. After that, you can explore Japan's famous cultural cities: Toyama, Kanazawa, Kyoto, Nara, and Osaka.
This plan combines the Alpine Route—where the journey is part of the experience—with time to enjoy gardens, museums, and temples, as well as to walk through lively cities. You can appreciate both nature and city life at a relaxed pace. This itinerary is suitable for everyone, from first-time visitors to those who have been to Japan before, providing an enjoyable experience for all.

Hotel Check-out

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>

After sightseeing at your own pace in Toyama,  travel from Toyama to Kanazawa by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in
 
Kanazawa is a city that keeps the feel of an Edo-period castle town while also featuring modern art and architecture. If you have extra time, explore more of Kanazawa. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots in Kanazawa>  
- Higashi Chaya District: Enjoy a magical atmosphere in the evening. It’s a great place for a stroll.

itinerary.description:

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kanazawa.

- Kenroku-en Garden: Explore one of Japan's Three Great Gardens, which offers beautiful views in every season.
- Kanazawa Castle Park: This park, next to Kenroku-en, has castle ruins and a large area to walk around.
- 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art: Check out this museum that showcases contemporary art, making it a great stop during your city walk.

Optional chartered taxi tour to Shirakawa-go (gassho-style village, a UNESCO World Heritage Site) is available from Kanazawa for an additional charge.
Maximum 3 passengers per vehicle. Advance reservation is required.

 Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.

- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this World Heritage temple and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

After breakfast, check out of the hotel and send your large luggage to Osaka. This lets you explore Kii-Katsuura freely.

Take a local train to Ise Shrine (NAIKU), Japan's most famous shrine with about 2,000 years of history. It is a peaceful place where you can reflect as you walk along the tree-lined path.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Naiku (Inner Shrine)→This is the main part of Ise Grand Shrine, where Amaterasu Omikami is honored. You will see beautiful sights like Uji Bridge and the Isuzu River.
★Okage Yokocho→This street has buildings from the Edo and Meiji periods. You can try local dishes like Ise udon and Akafuku mochi.

After your visit, take a kintetsu limited express to Matsusaka Station. From there, transfer to Kii-Katsuura using limited express trains.

Upon arrival at Kii-Katsuura Station, walk to Katsuura port and take the shuttle boat to the hotel.

Hotel check-in and Dinner at the hotel.

★Kumano Nachi Taisha Shrine→Visit this important shrine located in a deep forest, where you can feel a sense of peace.
★Nachi Falls→See Japan's Highest Drop waterfall, which drops 133 meters. The view from the observation deck is stunning.

After sightseeing, return to the hotel by chartered taxi.
Dinner at the hotel.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included

Day 2 in Osaka: More Tourist Spots to Explore!

tour.title: Alpine Wonders of Central Japan
tour.subtitle: Spring-Only Spectacle: Tateyama Snow Wall - April & May 2027
tour.description:
This nature course lasts about 1 month and lets you experience Snow Wall, a highlight of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route in spring.
You will travel through famous landscapes like Mount Fuji, Kamikochi, and the Japanese Alps. The journey ends with a stunning experience: walking through a snow wall several meters high.
This itinerary combines the exciting mountainous areas with the calm beauty of lakes and highlands, plus the relaxation of hot springs. You can fully enjoy the unique aspects of Japan that spring offers.
This is an excellent Alpine Route experience for those who want to feel the scale and power of nature during this season.
*The Tateyama Snow Wall is a seasonal landscape visible for about one month, typically from April to May each year.
tour.shortDescription: 12-day spring alpine tour (Apr–May): Mt Fuji, Kamikochi, Shirakawa-go, and Tateyama's famous 20-metre snow corridor. A seasonal spectacle.
highlights: The Tateyama Snow Wall Walk: A lovely path tucked between impressive, towering walls of snow.
Lake Kawaguchi offers beautiful views of Mount Fuji and the Arakura Fuji Sengen Shrine.
Matsumoto Castle, a National Treasure, stands proudly in its historic castle town.
In Chubu Sangaku National Park, you can explore the clear streams and mountain landscapes of Kamikochi.
Visit Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with traditional Gassho-zukuri farmhouses
Experience the stunning mountains by taking the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route.

itinerary.title: Mount Fuji Views & Lakeside Relaxation
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Matsumoto. You can explore Mount Fuji and Ustukushigahara at your leisure.

Take the chartered taxi to Mount Fuji.
Enjoy the beautiful views of Mount Fuji, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has shaped Japanese culture.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Arakura Fuji Sengen Shrine: This scenic spot represents Japan and offers great views of the five-story pagoda and Mount Fuji.
- Lake Kawaguchi: This popular spot lets you see Mount Fuji's changing beauty throughout the seasons from the lakeshore.
- Oshino Hakkai: This site has eight spring pools fed by Mount Fuji, each with its own unique water scenery.

After sightseeing, take the chartered taxi to Isawa Onsen.
Hotel Check-in

Isawa Onsen is one of the largest hot spring resorts in Yamanashi, located near the Mount Fuji area.

Relax and enjoy the hotel's hot springs.
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Sacred Shrines & Scenic Highlands of Nagano
Matsumoto Castle & Traditional Streets
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, let's enjoy sightseeing in Matsumoto.
Matsumoto is a town known for its castle and is surrounded by mountains. The main attraction is Matsumoto Castle, a National Treasure that represents the town. This area offers a mix of history, culture, nature, and city walks.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Matsumoto Castle: A beautiful castle with a black lacquered keep, symbolizing the town.
- Nakamachi Street: A street with white-walled storehouses, cafes, and craft shops.
- Former Kaichi School: This building is a National Treasure and an Important Cultural Property from the Meiji era. It shows the history of modern education in Japan.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Kamikochi: The Heart of the Japanese Alps
Shirakawa-go: Thatched Roof Villages
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Take the chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take the chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: From Mountain Towns to the Sea of Japan
Walk the Snow Walls: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route
Meet Japan’s Wild Monkeys in Nagano
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After check out, take the hotel shuttle bus to visit the Monkey Park.
Jigokudani Monkey Park is a special place where you can see wild Japanese macaques. The park also has nature trails where you can enjoy seasonal plants, streams, and the forest's beauty. This makes it a great spot to connect with both wildlife and nature.

After your visit, take the limited express train from Yudanaka to Nagano.

You have two sightseeing options: Plan A and Plan B.
[Plan A]
When you arrive at Nagano, enjoy lunch before taking the Shinkansen.
[Plan B]
Enjoy approximately two hours of free time to explore Zenko-ji Temple.
Zenko-ji Temple is a historic Buddhist temple dating back over 1,400 years.

In the afternoon, travel from Nagano to Tokyo by limited express train, then transfer to Shinjuku by local train.
Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?
Here are some great spots to check out.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for spending the last 12 days with our tour. 
We hope to see you again!

tour.title: Alpine Routes & Cultural Japan
tour.subtitle: Spring-Only Spectacle: Tateyama Snow Wall - April & May 2027
tour.description:
This tour combines nature and culture. It features a scenic mountain route through the Japanese Alps and visits historic cities in the Hokuriku and Kansai regions.
The main attraction is the "Snow Wall" on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, which you can only see in spring. Walking between snow walls over ten meters tall is a unique experience and the highlight of this trip.
You will travel from Tokyo through Nagano, crossing the Alpine Route and enjoying beautiful views at Murodo and Mikurigaike. You can also explore Japan's cultural cities: Toyama, Kanazawa, Kyoto, Nara, and Osaka.
This spring-only route lets you experience the impressive snow wall and stunning mountain scenery, along with gardens, temples, shrines, and city strolls. It offers a perfect mix of nature and urban life.
tour.shortDescription: Experience the spring-only Yuki-no-Otani snow corridor on the Tateyama Alpine Route, and explore Matsumoto, Kanazawa & Kyoto. Spring-only 11-day tour.
highlights: Experience the stunning mountains by taking the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route.
Walking between snow walls over ten meters tall at their peak is a unique experience and the highlight of this trip.
Visit High-altitude highlights such as Murodo and Mikurigaike Pond
Explore Toyama and Kanazawa freely in the Hokuriku region.
Walk through the temples, shrines, and streets of Kyoto and Osaka at your own pace.
Enjoy a route that combines the beauty of Japan's Alps with famous city sights.

Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Kanazawa. You can explore Matsumoto and Toyama at your leisure.

itinerary.title: Walk the Snow Walls: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route
Exploring the Hokuriku cities- Toyama & Kanazawa
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Toyama is a beautiful city surrounded by the Sea of Japan and the Northern Alps. You can easily take day trips from the city center to the mountains, the sea, and historic towns.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Toyama City Museum of Glass: This museum, located in central Toyama City, features modern architecture and beautiful glass art.

After sightseeing at your own pace in Toyama,  travel from Toyama to Kanazawa by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in
 
Kanazawa is a city that keeps the feel of an Edo-period castle town while also featuring modern art and architecture. If you have extra time, explore more of Kanazawa. 

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots in Kanazawa>  
- Higashi Chaya District: Enjoy a magical atmosphere in the evening. It’s a great place for a stroll. 
- Korinbo/Katamachi Area: This lively district is perfect for dining. Try local dishes like seafood and oden.

itinerary.title: Kanazawa: Gardens, Arts & Samurai Heritage
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kanazawa.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Omi-cho Market: Visit this market to enjoy local food, especially fresh seafood.
- Kenroku-en Garden: Explore one of Japan's Three Great Gardens, which offers beautiful views in every season.
- Kanazawa Castle Park: This park, next to Kenroku-en, has castle ruins and a large area to walk around.
- 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art: Check out this museum that showcases contemporary art, making it a great stop during your city walk.

Optional chartered taxi tour to Shirakawa-go (gassho-style village, a UNESCO World Heritage Site) is available from Kanazawa for an additional charge.
Maximum 3 passengers per vehicle. Advance reservation is required.

itinerary.title: Exploring Kyoto’s Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Kyoto at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kanazawa to Tsuruga by Shinkansen, then transfer to Kyoto by limited express train.

 Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this World Heritage temple and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we will take a longer trip to explore Kyoto’s famous sights.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that is beautifully gold-plated.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Timeless Nara, Dynamic Osaka
Free Exploration of Vibrant Osaka

Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Osaka!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

Thank you for joining our 11-day tour.
We look forward to seeing you again.

Explore the islands of Shodoshima, Naoshima, and Teshima in Takamatsu. Walk through the historic streets of Okayama and Kurashiki, and don’t miss Himeji Castle. 
End your journey by unwinding in the hot springs of Kinosaki Onsen. This trip provides a fantastic experience of the Seto Inland Sea and its famous hot springs.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Okayama by Shinkansen, then take the limited express train to Kotohira.

Enjoy free time for sightseeing.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Kotohira-gu Shrine: The main attraction with 785 stone steps.  
- Omotesando: A charming street with historic inns and shops.  
- Sanuki Udon: Kagawa’s specialty, known for its handmade texture.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel
Relax in the hot springs to unwind

itinerary.title: Adventure in the Hidden Iya Valley and Ritsurin Garden
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Join a morning bus tour to Iya Valley and Oboke.  
Both areas feature beautiful mountains, steep gorges, and clear streams.  
- Oboke Gorge: Known for its tall rock walls and stunning views.  
- Kazura Bridge: A vine-woven bridge popular for its thrilling sway.
*For tours departing between November 28 and February 25, the Iya Valley & Oboke Shuttle Bus Tour is unavailable and will be replaced with free time for independent sightseeing.

In the afternoon, travel from Kotoden Kotohira to Ritsurin-Kouen and transfer to Takamatsu-chikko.
We recommend exploring Takamatsu, a coastal city known for its history, art, and food.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Ritsurin Garden: A beautiful garden ideal for a relaxing walk.  
- Takamatsu Castle Ruins (Tamamo Park): Explore the castle foundations and stone walls.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Experiencing Life on the Islands of the Seto Inland Sea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

In the morning, travel from Takamatsu Port to Tonosho Port by ferry.

Shodoshima is a quiet island in the Seto Inland Sea, known for olives and soy sauce. 
Local drivers provide guided taxi tours to explore the island.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Angel Road: A sandbar that appears at low tide; legend says crossing it while holding hands grants wishes.
- Shodoshima Olive Park: A scenic spot with olive groves and ocean views.
- Soy Sauce Brewery Area: See traditional soy sauce made in wooden barrels.
- Kankakei Ropeway: Enjoy stunning views of the gorges from above.
- Nakayama Senmaida Terraces: Beautiful terraced rice fields with stone walls.

itinerary.title: Island of Contemporary Art- Naoshima island
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

In the morning,travel from Takamatsu Port to Miyaura Port by ferry.

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring.
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape.
- Explore art installations in preserved homes.
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea.
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

Travel back  to Takamatsu Port by ferry.

itinerary.title: A Flexible Day Exploring the Setouchi Islands
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

The Seto Inland Sea is a beautiful area with unique islands full of art, nature, and history. Plan your trip carefully, as museum hours and ferry schedules vary by island.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Teshima: A calm island with natural beauty and traditional houses. Visit the museum to experience nature through water, sound, and light, and walk the terraced rice fields.
- Inujima: An island focused on art and industrial heritage, featuring the Inujima "Dog Project."
- Ogijima & Megijima: These islands combine daily life with art. You'll find artworks throughout.
- Yashima: A scenic viewpoint in Takamatsu City with a nice path around the Shikoku Mura Museum.

itinerary.title: The Land of Sunshine – Okayama & Kurashiki
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Okayama, Himeji and Kinosaki at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Takamatsu to Okayama by limited express train.

Okayama and Kurashiki are rich in history and culture. Kurashiki features charming white-walled streets, while Okayama has notable castles and gardens.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter: A great spot for walking with beautiful streets, cafes, and shops.
- Ohara Museum of Art: A top museum with famous artworks, including pieces by Monet.
- Okayama Castle: Known for its black exterior, it offers stunning views from the tower.
- Korakuen Garden: A beautiful Japanese garden and one of Japan's Three Great Gardens.

In the afternoon, travel from Okayama to Himeji by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Himeji Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Journey to Hot Spring Town Kinosaki
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel  
Hotel Check-out

Himeji is a beautiful castle town with rich history. Before we leave, let’s sightsee.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Himeji Castle: One of Japan's most beautiful castles and a World Heritage site. Climb the steep stairs for a great view of Himeji City.

Around noon, travel from Himeji to Kinosaki Onsen by limited express train.  
Enjoy a relaxing day in Kinosaki Onsen, a picturesque hot spring town with wooden hotels and willow trees.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit the Public Baths: Enjoy seven hot springs with a bath pass. A yukata is recommended for strolling.
- Amusement Arcade: Visit for games like smart ball and shooting galleries, with different vibes day and night.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Morning in Kinosaki Onsen and the Flavors of Osaka at Night
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Let's take some time to explore Kinosaki Onsen!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Explore the Onsen Town: Discover cafes and souvenir shops along the charming streets.
- Kinosaki Onsen Ropeway: Ride the ropeway for great views of Kinosaki town and the Sea of Japan.

Around noon, travel from Kinosaki Onsen to Osaka by limited express train. 

Osaka is lively, with busy neighborhoods and a rich food culture.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Dotonbori & Shinsaibashi: Enjoy bright signs and street food like takoyaki.
- Umeda Sky Building: Visit the observatory for a 360-degree view of Osaka, especially beautiful at night.

itinerary.title: The adventure kicks off in vibrant Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Heading West by Bullet Train- Old Port Town Tomonoura
Historic Coastal Towns and the Peaceful City of Hiroshima
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Let’s do some sightseeing in Tomonoura before we leave.  

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots in Tomonoura> 
- Ota Family Residence: A historic merchant's home showcasing traditional architecture.  
- Fukusenji Temple Taishiro Hall: Offers great views of Sensuijima Island.  

Around noon, travel from the Hotel in Tomonoura to Fukuyama by hotel's shuttle bus, then transfer to Hiroshima by Shinkansen.

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.
Let's spend more time exploring Hiroshima.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): A UNESCO World Heritage Site representing the impact of war.
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.
- Okonomimura & Hiroshima Station Area: Known for Hiroshima's famous okonomiyaki.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Sacred Island of Japan- Miyajima
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Travel to Miyajima by train and ferry.
Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an "island of the gods."
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

itinerary.title: Hidden Streets of Takehara and Sake Culture of Japan
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Takamatsu. You can explore Takehara, Onomichi and Kurashiki at your leisure.

In the mornng, travel from Hiroshima to the Takehara Historic Town Preservation District by express bus.
Takehara is a charming historic town, known for its beautifully preserved streets and traditional buildings.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takehara Historic Town Preservation District: Takehara is a quiet port town with white-walled merchant houses and sake breweries, showcasing a traditional Japanese atmosphere.
- Preservation District: Walk through this area to see historic buildings from the Edo period.
- Taketsuru Distillery: Visit the sake brewery associated with Masataka Taketsuru, known for its historic buildings.
- Fumeikaku: This temple offers great views of Takehara.

In the afternoon, travel from Takehara to Onomichi by local train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Exploring the Coastal Temple Town of Onomichi
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Onomichi is a beautiful port town between the sea and mountains. It has sloping streets, temples, and retro buildings that create a rich atmosphere.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Senkoji Temple: Take the ropeway to the top of the mountain for stunning views of the Onomichi Channel. Enjoy the calm surroundings in Senkoji Park and walk along the Literary Path.
- Onomichi Ramen: Try the local ramen. It has a light, soy sauce-based broth that is easy to enjoy.
- Setoda Stroll: You can reach Ikuchijima Island by ferry from Onomichi Port. Explore the Shio Machi Shopping Street and enjoy the coastal views.
- Kosanji Temple: This temple in Setoda is famous for its beautiful decorations. It offers a unique look at the scenery and culture of the Seto Inland Sea.

itinerary.title: White-Walled Streets and Art- From Kurashiki to Takamatsu
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out  

In the morning, travel from Onomichi to Kurashiki by local train. 

 Kurashiki is a historic area with beautiful white-walled buildings.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter: A great spot for walking with beautiful streets, cafes, and shops.
- Ohara Museum of Art: A top museum with famous artworks, including pieces by Monet.

In the afternoon, travel from Kurashiki to Okayama by local train, then transfer to Takamatsu by rapid train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Experiencing Life on the Islands of the Seto Islands Sea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

In the morning, travel from Takamatsu Port to Tonosho Port by ferry.

Shodoshima is a quiet island in the Seto Inland Sea, known for olives and soy sauce.
Local drivers provide guided taxi tours to explore the island.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Angel Road: A sandbar that appears at low tide; legend says crossing it while holding hands grants wishes.
- Shodoshima Olive Park: A scenic spot with olive groves and ocean views.
- Soy Sauce Brewery Area: See traditional soy sauce made in wooden barrels.
- Kankakei Ropeway: Enjoy stunning views of the gorges from above.
- Nakayama Senmaida Terraces: Beautiful terraced rice fields with stone walls.

itinerary.title: Island of Contemporary Art- Naoshima
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

In the morning,travel from Takamatsu Port to Miyaura Port by ferry.

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring.
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape.
- Explore art installations in preserved homes.
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea.
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

Travel back to Takamatsu Port by ferry.

itinerary.title: A Flexible Day Exploring the Setouchi Islands
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

The Seto Inland Sea is a beautiful area with unique islands full of art, nature, and history. Plan your trip carefully, as museum hours and ferry schedules vary by island.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Teshima: A calm island with natural beauty and traditional houses. Visit the museum to experience nature through water, sound, and light, and walk the terraced rice fields.
- Inujima: An island focused on art and industrial heritage, featuring the Inujima "Dog Project."
- Ogijima & Megijima: These islands combine daily life with art. You'll find artworks throughout.
- Yashima: A scenic viewpoint in Takamatsu City with a nice path around the Shikoku Mura Museum.

itinerary.title: The Sea God Konpira, Scenic Gardens and Onsen Relaxation
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Kotohira at your leisure. 

In the morning, travel from Takamatsu-chikko to Ritsurin-Kouen by local train.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Ritsurin Garden: This Japanese garden is known for its beautiful views throughout the seasons. Enjoy a peaceful walk around the pond.

Around noon, travel from Ritsurin-Kouen to Kotoden Kotohira.
Kotohira is famous for the Kotohira-gu Shrine, which honors sea guardians. Climbing the stone steps may bring blessings. Explore traditional buildings and local food.
Enjoy free time for sightseeing.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kotohira-gu Shrine: The main attraction with 785 stone steps.
- Omotesando: A charming street with historic inns and shops.
- Sanuki Udon: Kagawa’s specialty, known for its handmade texture.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel
Relax in the hot springs to unwind

itinerary.title: Adventure in the Hidden Iya Valley and the Flavors of Osaka at Night
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Join a morning bus tour to Iya Valley and Oboke.
Both areas feature beautiful mountains, steep gorges, and clear streams.
- Oboke Gorge: Known for its tall rock walls and stunning views.
- Kazura Bridge: A vine-woven bridge popular for its thrilling sway.
*For tours departing between November 28 and February 25, the Iya Valley & Oboke Shuttle Bus Tour is unavailable and will be replaced with free time for independent sightseeing.

In the afternoon, travel from Kotohira to Okayama by limited express train, then transfer to Osaka by Shinkansen and local train.

Osaka is lively, with busy neighborhoods and a rich food culture.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Dotonbori & Shinsaibashi: Enjoy bright signs and street food like takoyaki.
- Umeda Sky Building: Visit the observatory for a 360-degree view of Osaka, especially beautiful at night.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Free Exploration of Vibrant Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Osaka.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

itinerary.title: Sayonara- Until We Meet Again in Japan!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel.
The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for spending the last 15 days with our tour. 
We hope to see you again!

- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Head to Himeji and explore at your own pace
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tamatsukuri-Onsen. You can explore Himeji, Tottori and Matsue at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Himeji by Shinkansen.

Himeji is a beautiful castle town with rich history.
Enjoy sightseeing in Himeji!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Himeji Castle: Admire the beauty of a UNESCO World Heritage Site of Himeji Castle and be sure not to miss the spectacular nighttime illumination.
- Koko-en: This Japanese garden located on the west side of Himeji Castle is a beautifully designed space established on the site of a former Edo-period mansion. Visitors can appreciate the garden’s seasonal landscapes, and matcha tasting is also offered for an authentic cultural experience.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: The vast beauty of the Tottori Sand Dunes
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Himeji to Tottori by limited express train.
Tottori is famous for its spectacular sand dunes and beautiful coastal scenery, offering a unique landscape unlike anywhere else in Japan.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Tottori Sand Dunes: Japan's largest coastal sand dunes, offering vast golden landscapes and panoramic views of the Sea of Japan. 
- The Sand Museum: A unique museum featuring impressive sand sculptures created by artists from around the world. 
- Tottori Sand Dunes Lift: Enjoy scenic views of the dunes and coastline from above as you ride the lift.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Experiencing the harmony of art and gardens
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Tottori to Yasugi by limited express train and head to Adachi Museum by shuttle bus.

Adachi Museum of Art is renowned for its beautiful Japanese garden and impressive collection of Japanese art.
Enjoy a peaceful day surrounded by nature and art!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> 
- Adachi Museum of Art: Admire the world-famous Japanese garden and explore its collection of paintings and ceramics.

In the afternoon, travel from Adachi Museum to Yasugi by shuttle bus and transfer to Matsue by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: A journey through Izumo and Matsue’s timeless heritage
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, take a chartered taxi for sightseeing in Matsue.
Matsue is a charming castle town surrounded by beautiful lakes, gardens, and traditional hot springs.
Enjoy sightseeing in Matsue!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
 - Matsue Castle: One of Japan's original surviving castles, offering beautiful views of the city and surrounding moats. 
- Yuushien Garden: A stunning Japanese garden famous for its beautiful peony displays. 
- Izumo Taisha Grand Shrine: One of Japan's most important shrines, famous for its giant shimenawa rope and connection to matchmaking. 
- Tamatsukuri Onsen: A historic hot spring resort known as the "hot spring of beautiful skin," with traditional ryokan along the river.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel
Relax in the hot springs to unwind

itinerary.title: White-Walled Streets and Art in Kurashiki
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Kurashiki, Naoshima and Okayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tamatsukuri-Onsen to Kurashiki by limited express train.

Kurashiki is a historic area with beautiful white-walled buildings.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter: A great spot for walking with beautiful streets, cafes, and shops.
- Ohara Museum of Art: A top museum with famous artworks, including pieces by Monet.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Island of Contemporary Art- Naoshima island
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the hotel

In the morning,travel from Kurashiki to Uno by local train and rapid train, then transfer to Miyaura Port by ferry.

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring.
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape.
- Explore art installations in preserved homes.
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea.
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

Travel back to Kurashiki by ferry and local train.

itinerary.title: A day in Okayama before heading to Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Kurashiki to Okayama by local train.
Okayama is rich in history and culture, such as notable castles and gardens.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Okayama Castle: Known for its black exterior, it offers stunning views from the tower.
- Korakuen Garden: A beautiful Japanese garden and one of Japan's Three Great Gardens.

In the afternoon, travel from Okayama to Osaka by Shinkansen and local train.

Osaka is lively, with busy neighborhoods and a rich food culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Osaka!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Dotonbori & Shinsaibashi: Enjoy bright signs and street food like takoyaki.
- Umeda Sky Building: Visit the observatory for a 360-degree view of Osaka, especially beautiful at night.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Free Exploration of Vibrant Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Osaka.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

itinerary.title: Sayonara- Until We Meet Again in Japan!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for spending the last 11 days with our tour. 
We hope to see you again!

You have two sightseeing options: Plan A and Plan B.

[Plan A]  
Transfer to Kanazawa and enjoy free time for sightseeing.
We recommended visiting the following areas:
★Higashi Chaya District→Enjoy a magical atmosphere in the evening. It’s a great place for a stroll. 
★Korinbo/Katamachi Area→This lively district is perfect for dining. Try local dishes like seafood and oden.

[Plan B]  
Enjoy approximately two hours of free time to explore Zenko-ji Temple.  Zenko-ji Temple is a historic Buddhist temple dating back over 1,400 years.
After your visit, take Shinkansen from Nagano Station to Kanazawa Station.

itinerary.title: Kanazawa: Gardens, Arts & Samurai Heritage
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast in Hotel.

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kanazawa.
Kanazawa is a city that keeps the feel of an Edo-period castle town while also featuring modern art and architecture.

We recommend visiting the following areas *Entrance fees not included
★Omi-cho Market→Visit this market to enjoy local food, especially fresh seafood.
★Kenroku-en Garden→Explore one of Japan's Three Great Gardens, which offers beautiful views in every season.
★Kanazawa Castle Park→This park, next to Kenroku-en, has castle ruins and a large area to walk around.
★21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art→Check out this museum that showcases contemporary art, making it a great stop during your city walk.

Optional private taxi tour to Shirakawa-go (UNESCO World Heritage gassho-style village) is available from Kanazawa. (9:00–16:00)
Advance reservation request is required.

itinerary.title: Exploring Kyoto’s Historic Streets
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast in Hotel.

In the morning, travel from Kanazawa Station to Tsuruga by Shinkansen, then transfer to Kyoto Station by limited express train.
🚅Kanazawa Station→Kyoto Station

 Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.

We recommend visiting the following areas *Entrance fees not included
★Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka→Visit this World Heritage temple and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
★Gion and Yasaka Shrine→Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
★Stroll along the Kamo River→This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

Hotel check-in

itinerary.title: Kyoto Icons: Timeless Sights of the Ancient Capital
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast in Hotel.

Today, we will take a longer trip to explore Kyoto’s famous sights.

We recommend visiting the following areas *Entrance fees not included
★Kinkaku-ji Temple→A beautiful World Heritage site that is gold-plated.
★Arashiyama→A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
★Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine→A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
★Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi→An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Head to Hakone and more than just a spa!
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast in Hotel.
Check-out and have your large luggage shipped to Tokyo, so you can explore Hakone without heavy bags.  

In the morning, go to Kyoto Station and take the Shinkansen to Odawara.
🚅Kyoto Station→Odawara Station

Use the Hakone Free Pass to reach Hakone-Yumoto Station. 

We recommend visiting the following areas *Entrance fees not included
★Owakudani→Volcanic area with steaming vents and black eggs.  
★Lake Ashi→Enjoy beautiful nature and Mount Fuji.  

Hotel check-in

Dinner will be at the hotel. Afterward, relax in the hot spring baths and enjoy the famous Miyanoshita Onsen while taking in the natural beauty around you.

itinerary.title: Explore at your own pace in Hakone
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast in Hotel.

Hakone is a popular hot spring destination in Japan, known for its views of Mount Fuji and great dining. 

We recommend visiting the following areas *Entrance fees not included
★Hakone Open-Air Museum→Art in the natural landscape.  
★Togendai→Lunch with views of Lake Ashi and Mount Fuji.  
★The Old Highway Cedar Avenue→Lined with historic cedar trees. 

You can also visit Hakone Gora Park, the Hakone Venetian Glass Museum, and Sengokuhara Susuki Grass Field with the Hakone Free Pass. 

After sightseeing at your own pace in Hakone,  take the Hakone Free Pass to Odawara Station. From there, board the Shinkansen to Tokyo Station.
🚅Odawara Station→Tokyo Station(Non-reserved seat)

itinerary.title: Tradition and Modern Life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast in Hotel.

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

We recommend visiting the following areas *Entrance fees not included
★Asakusa→This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
★TOKYO SKYTREE®→A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
★The Imperial Palace→A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
★Omotesando→A shopping street known for its luxury brand boutiques and unique architecture.
★Shibuya Scramble Crossing→A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
★Harajuku→An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Sayonara- Until We Meet Again
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast in Hotel.
The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for spending the last 13 days with our tour. 
We hope to see you again!

tour.title: Japan Winter Journey with Ski and Cities
tour.subtitle: Gear Included for Easy Skiing
tour.description:
This winter tour is perfect for enjoying skiing, soaking in Japanese hot springs, and exploring historic towns. First, you will visit Nagano, where you can see the famous wild monkeys bathing in hot springs surrounded by snow. Afterwards, you will stay at Yudanaka Onsen and spend a day skiing at Shiga Kogen Ski Resort. Your transportation to the ski resort is included for a stress-free experience.
Next, you will explore Takayama, an old town that still has its Edo-period charm. You will also visit Shirakawa-go, a village recognized as a World Heritage site for its thatched-roof gassho-zukuri houses. A taxi will take you around to enjoy the beautiful winter scenery showcasing Japan's traditional landscapes.
To make your trip easier, we include ski gear rental, so you don’t have to carry it. We also offer parcel delivery services for transfers between cities, allowing you to travel comfortably. This ski trip combines fun snow activities with Japanese culture and is suitable for beginners.
tour.shortDescription: 9-day Japan winter tour: ski at Shiga Kogen with gear included, see snow monkeys, and explore Takayama and Shirakawa-go.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast at the Hotel
When you check-out, please send your large luggage to Tokyo. This way, you can explore Takayama without heavy bags. 

After check-out, transfer by hotel's shuttle bus service to Yudanaka Station. Travel from Yudanaka Station to Nagano Station by Nagano Dentetsu Limited express train,  transfer to Takayama Station by the Shinkansen and Limited Express Train .
🚃Yudanaka Station→Nagano Station
🚅Nagano Station→Toyama Station
🚃Toyama Station→Takayama Station

Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>  *Entrance fees not included
★Takayama Jinya→This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
★Old Town (Sanmachi Street)→This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.

After your exploration, check-in at your hotel.
Diinner at hotel

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go: Thatched Roof Villages
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast at the Hotel

Take a chatered taxi for a day trip to Shirakawa-go, a World Heritage site. Shirakawa-go is a village with gassho-zukuri houses, which are notable for their steep, thatched roofs. This village keeps the traditional look and way of life of a Japanese mountain community.

After your visit, return to the hotel by a chartered taxi. (Fare included)

itinerary.title: Exploring  Nagoya and then heading back to Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast at the Hotel

Check-out and take Limited Express Train to Nagoya.
🚃Takayama Station→Nagoya Station

Nagoya is a beautiful city full of samurai history and unique food. A short trip to Inuyama lets you see Inuyama Castle, a national treasure, and the historic castle town by the Kiso River.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Nagoya Castle→This is the symbol of Nagoya, known for its golden shachihoko ornaments. 
★Noritake Forest→Here, you can learn about the history of ceramics and craftsmanship. 
★Osu Shopping District→Explore this lively area, which combines old shops with a youthful vibe. 

After sightseeing in Nagoya,  board the Shinkansen to Tokyo.
🚅Nagoya Station→Tokyo Station

Hotel check-in

itinerary.title: Tradition and Modern Life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots> *Entrance fees not included
★Asakusa→This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
★TOKYO SKYTREE®→A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
★The Imperial Palace→A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
★Omotesando→A shopping street known for its luxury brand boutiques and unique architecture.
★Shibuya Scramble Crossing→A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
★Harajuku→An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Sayonara- Until We Meet Again
itinerary.description:
Enjoy breakfast at the Hotel. The tour ends at hotel check-out.
Thank you for spending the last 9 days with our tour. 
We hope to see you again!

tour.title: Hakuba Misorano & Zao with Snow Monkeys
tour.subtitle: Ski Resort Hopping: Premium Room Plan
tour.description:
This tour includes a total of four nights in Tokyo and visits to the ski resorts of Hakuba Misorano and Zao. You will also visit Yudanaka Onsen and the Snow Monkey Park, where you can observe wild Japanese macaques bathing in natural hot springs. 
Hakuba Happo-One Ski Resort in Hakuba Village, Nagano Prefecture, is one of Japan’s premier ski destinations. Featuring diverse runs with spectacular views of the Northern Alps, the resort offers enjoyable skiing and snowboarding for beginners and advanced riders alike.
Zao Onsen Ski Resort in Yamagata Prefecture is renowned for its iconic “Snow Monsters” and diverse terrain across 14 slopes and 12 courses, suitable for all levels.

itinerary.title: The adventure kicks off in vibrant Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

This vibrant city beautifully blends traditional Japanese culture with the latest trends. The best way to experience all that Tokyo has to offer is by exploring on foot, so put on your walking shoes and get ready for an adventure!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Asakusa: This traditional downtown area preserves old-world charm and features iconic sites such as the Kaminarimon Gate and Sensoji Temple.
- Tokyo Skytree®: A popular destination that offers panoramic views of Tokyo from its observation deck.
- The Imperial Palace: A serene location surrounded by beautiful gardens and historic buildings.
- Shibuya Scramble Crossing: A bustling symbol of Tokyo, filled with people.
- Harajuku: An area where youth culture and unique fashion come together.

itinerary.title: Travel to Nagoya & Castle Town Exploration
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Nagoya and Kashikojima at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Tokyo to Nagoya by Shinkansen.

Nagoya is a beautiful city full of samurai history and unique food.
Enjoy sightseeing in Nagoya!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nagoya Castle: This is the symbol of Nagoya, known for its golden shachihoko ornaments.
- Noritake Forest: Here, you can learn about the history of ceramics and craftsmanship.
- Osu Shopping District: Explore this lively area, which combines old shops with a youthful vibe.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Toba's Ama diving culture and the delicious seafood
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Nagoya to Toba by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

Toba is a port town in Mie Prefecture. It is known for its beautiful sea and island views and for its Ama diving culture.

From Toba, take the shuttle bus to Hachiman Kamado.
Hachiman Kamado is an Ama hut where you can enjoy a meal while Ama divers share stories about their fishing experiences and lives. You will enjoy delicious Ise seafood for lunch!

After lunch, take the shuttle bus back to Toba, then travel from Toba to Kashikojima by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in
Dinner at the Hotel

itinerary.title: Refined Shima – Pearls, Sea & Culture
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, board the Kashikojima España Cruise, and take in the full beauty of Ago Bay.

Around noon, travel from Kashikojima to Toba by limited express train.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Mikimoto Pearl Island: This is where the first successful pearl cultivation happened. Here, you can learn about the history of pearl farming. Watch live demonstrations by Ama divers and shop for beautiful pearl jewelry.

Travel from Toba to Osaka Namba by Sightseeing Limited Express "SHIMAKAZE" or another limited express train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: History, Views, and Food in Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Osaka is lively, with busy neighborhoods and a rich food culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Osaka!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

itinerary.title: Day trip to Koyasan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the spiritual center of Shingon Buddhism
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

In the morning, move to Koyasan by limited express train.

Koyasan is a mountain town recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
It is surrounded by cedar forests and has deep ties to Japanese Buddhism. Kobo Daishi Kukai practiced asceticism here for over 1,200 years.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Danjo Garan: This is the main area of Koyasan. You can see the famous Konpon Daito Pagoda and Kondo Hall here, which create a beautiful landscape.
- Strolling the Approach: Walk through the calm mountain town, which has souvenir shops and stores that sell Buddhist altar goods.
- Kongobuji Temple: This is the main temple of Koyasan Shingon Buddhism. It features one of Japan’s largest rock gardens, perfect for quiet reflection.

In the evening, return to Osaka by limited express train.

itinerary.title: Discovering the Timeless Charm of Nara and transfer to Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Nara and Kyoto at your leisure.
In the morning, travel from Osaka to Nara by Sightseeing Limited Express "AONIYOSHI", or another limited express train.

Nara is one of Japan's oldest cultural centers, filled with ancient temples, historic shrines, and peaceful parks.
Enjoy sightseeing in Nara!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Todai-ji Temple: The Daibutsuden Hall, home to the Great Buddha, is an impressive sight where you can experience the history and religious culture of Japan.
- Kasuga Taisha Shrine: Characterized by its vermilion-colored structures and more than a thousand stone lanterns.
- Kofuku-ji Temple: A historic temple featuring a graceful five-story pagoda.
- Nara Park: A vast park blending serene scenery with historic landmarks. Take a moment to interact with and feed the gentle deer that inhabit this unique area.

Transfer to Kyoto by limited express train.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Stepping into Kyoto's Timeless Traditions
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Kyoto is the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this World Heritage temple and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.

itinerary.title: Morning in Kyoto and Night life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Let’s continue sightseeing in Kyoto!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kinkaku-ji Temple: A beautiful World Heritage site that is gold-plated.
- Arashiyama: A popular tourist spot known for its bamboo grove and Togetsukyo Bridge. You can also enjoy a rickshaw ride here.
- Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine: A popular place for photos, featuring thousands of red torii gates.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

In the afternoon, travel from Kyoto to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in
Let's also enjoy the night life in Tokyo.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?

Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
The tour ends at hotel check-out.

Thank you for joining our 12-day tour.
We look forward to seeing you again.

After kicking off your journey in Tokyo, head away from the hustle and bustle to Koyasan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a sacred place in Japanese Buddhism.
In this place where Kukai's prayers from 1,200 years ago still linger, you can enjoy a relaxing experience through the solemn temple complex, the mystical atmosphere of the sacred site Okunoin, and a stay at a temple lodging.
In Kyoto, you can enjoy the beauty and delicacy of Japanese culture in the cityscape. In Takayama, you can experience the traditional wooden houses and simple mountain life, adding a gentle afterglow to your journey.  
This route, which emphasizes feeling rather than superficial sightseeing, is a luxurious journey that allows you to confront yourself. In the stillness, a deep sense of satisfaction resides.

Osaka is the place to go. Shop at Osaka's foremost shopping districts Dotonbori and Tsutenkaku Tower and indulge in takoyaki and okonomiyaki until your heart's content!

Nara is the place to be. Nara predates Kyoto as an ancient capital, and its UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Todaiji Temple, Kasuga Taisha Shrine, and Kofukuji Temple — are just some of many spots with a rich and immersive history.
Nara Park also provides a unique experience where feeding the gentle deer offers a moment to connect with nature.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Takayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Kyoto to Nagoya by Shinkansen, then take the limited express train to Takayama. 
Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.

Enjoy sightseeing in Takayama.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takayama Jinya: This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
- Old Town (Sanmachi Street): This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.
- Hida no Sato: This is an open-air museum featuring traditional Gassho style houses. Visitors can experience the original Japanese landscape of Gassho-zukuri farmhouses.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go: Thatched Roof Villages

Take a chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: Island of Contemporary Art- Naoshima

Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we recommend exploring popular islands known for their art.

Naoshima Island features museums and outdoor artworks, making it great for walking and exploring.
Reserve a rental bicycle in advance to get around easily.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Visit museums that blend with the sea and landscape.
- Explore art installations in preserved homes.
- Enjoy outdoor art with views of the Seto Inland Sea.
- Walk or bike the island, stopping at local cafes.

itinerary.title: Explore Okayama and Kurashiki, the Land of Sunshine
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Okayama and Kurashiki are rich in history and culture. Kurashiki features charming white-walled streets, while Okayama has notable castles and gardens.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kurashiki Bikan Historical Quarter: A great spot for walking with beautiful streets, cafes, and shops.
- Ohara Museum of Art: A top museum with famous artworks, including pieces by Monet.
- Okayama Castle: Known for its black exterior, it offers stunning views from the tower.
- Korakuen Garden: A beautiful Japanese garden and one of Japan's Three Great Gardens.

In the afternoon, travel from Okayama to Hiroshima by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Miyajima & the Sacred Shrine by the Sea
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Travel to Miyajima by train and ferry.

Miyajima is a beautiful island in Hiroshima Bay, known as an "island of the gods."
Enjoy a full day at Miyajima!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Itsukushima Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: A beautiful and mystifying red shrine suspended on the sea is a must-see!
- Otorii Gate: Watch as the sea tides surround this enormous torii gate. Observe the vibrant red-colored Senjo-kaku Pavilion, Five-story Pagoda and National Treasure Tahoto Pagoda also nearby.
- Daigan-ji Temple and Daisho-in Temple: Also in the area and may be of interest.
- Miyajima Ropeway: Time permitting, enjoy the view of Miyajima and the Inland Sea.
- Miyajima History and Folklore Museum and Miyajima Traditional Crafts Center: For those who enjoy history, the history and traditions of Miyajima can be learned here.

Travel back to Hiroshima by ferry and train.

itinerary.title: Reflecting on Hiroshima's history, then Transfer to Fukuoka

After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Osaka. You can explore Hiroshima city and Fukuoka at your leisure.

Hiroshima is rich in culture and easy to explore by streetcar, offering various attractions and local food.
Let's spend more time exploring Hiroshima.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome): A UNESCO World Heritage Site representing the impact of war.
- Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park: A park honoring atomic bomb victims, with a museum.
- Okonomimura & Hiroshima Station Area: Known for Hiroshima's famous okonomiyaki.

In the afternoon, travel from Hiroshima to Hakata by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in

Fukuoka is the gateway to Kyushu. It offers a mix of great food, history, and beautiful coastlines. Try local dishes like tonkotsu ramen, mentaiko, and motsunabe.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Tenjin/Hakata Night Yatai Hopping: Experience the local street food at yatai stalls. Enjoy options like ramen, yakitori, and oden.

itinerary.title: Let’s enjoy the delicious food and happy flavors of Fukuoka!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Let’s continue sightseeing in Fukuoka.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Ohori Park: Visit this lovely waterfront Park in the city center. Stroll around the pond or check out the nearby art museum and the ruins of Fukuoka Castle.
-Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine: Visit this famous shrine for the god of learning. Walk the traditional path and try the "Ume-ga-e Mochi" rice cakes.
- Itoshima Area: Explore this resort area with cafes, beaches, and craft shops.
- Munakata Area: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with ancient shrines and museums, where you can enjoy the sea and explore history.

itinerary.title: Free Exploration of Vibrant Osaka
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

In the morning, travel from Hakata to Shin-Osaka by Shinkansen.

Osaka is lively, with busy neighborhoods and a rich food culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Osaka!

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Dotonbori & Shinsaibashi: Enjoy bright signs and street food like takoyaki.
- Umeda Sky Building: Visit the observatory for a 360-degree view of Osaka, especially beautiful at night.
- Tennoji & Abeno Harukas: Visit Japan's tallest building for stunning views, shopping, and museums.
- Nakanoshima Area: Enjoy cultural sites along the river, perfect for art lovers and peaceful walks.
- Osaka Castle: Take in great views of Osaka from the castle tower.
- Shinsekai: Experience this retro district at Tsutenkaku Tower and try local foods like doteyaki and kushikatsu.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Wandering through the beautiful sights of Kyoto
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Today, we recommend exploring Kyoto, the heart of Japanese culture, filled with historic temples, shrines, and beautiful streets.
Enjoy sightseeing in Kyoto.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kiyomizu-dera Temple, Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka: Visit this UNESCO World Heritage Site and explore the souvenir shops and tea houses along the slopes.
- Gion and Yasaka Shrine: Walk through the charming streets of Gion. You might see a maiko (apprentice geisha) while you’re there.
- Stroll along the Kamo River: This is a great place for an evening walk. Enjoy a break at a riverside cafe.
- Nishiki Market & Kawaramachi: An area where you can try Kyoto’s food and do some shopping.

itinerary.title: Takayama Old Town
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
After breakfast, check out and send your large luggage to Tokyo. You can explore Takayama at your leisure.

In the morning, travel from Shin-Osaka to Nagoya by Shinkansen, then take the limited express train to Takayama.

Takayama is a historic mountain town with buildings from the Edo period. You can walk around and see traditional houses and local culture.
Enjoy sightseeing in Takayama.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Takayama Jinya: This historic building was a magistrate's office during the Edo period.
- Old Town (Sanmachi Street): This area has traditional machiya houses and is great for a nice walk.
- Hida no Sato: This is an open-air museum featuring traditional Gassho style houses. Visitors can experience the original Japanese landscape of Gassho-zukuri farmhouses.

Hotel Check-in

itinerary.title: Shirakawa-go and Timeless Village Life
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Take a chartered taxi to Shirakawa-go, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This traditional farming village showcases Gassho-zukuri thatched houses designed for harsh winters, preserving ancestral wisdom.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Gassho-zukuri Village: Steep roofs shed heavy snow, creating unique regional landscapes.
- Wada House: Large farmhouse displaying sericulture and traditional mountain life.
- Shirakawa-go Observatory: Panoramic village views revealing nature-human harmony.

After sightseeing, take a chartered taxi to Takayama.

itinerary.title: Morning in Takayama and Night life in Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
Hotel Check-out

Enjoy a morning in Takayama before departure.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Miyagawa Asaichi: Lively morning market with local specialties and crafts, where you can buy fresh foods.

In the afternoon, travel from Takayama to Nagoya by limited express train, then transfer to Tokyo by Shinkansen.

Hotel Check-in
Let's also enjoy the night life in Tokyo.

<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Nihonbashi/Ginza: A great area for shopping that blends tradition and modernity.

itinerary.title: Have fun in the friendly and relaxed neighborhoods of Tokyo
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel

Ready to explore beyond Tokyo?

Here are some great spots to check out:
<Recommended Sightseeing Spots>
- Kamakura: A lovely historic town with beautiful coastlines. Don’t miss the Great Buddha and a stroll down Komachi Street!
- Nikko: Perfect for nature and culture lovers, featuring the stunning Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Kegon Falls.
- Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi: Enjoy breathtaking views of Japan’s tallest mountain and the nearby lake.
Plus, there are exciting amusement and theme parks close by for some extra fun!

itinerary.title: Sayonara, and can't wait to see you next time!
itinerary.description:
Breakfast at the Hotel
The tour ends at hotel check-out.

Thank you for joining our 15-day tour.
We look forward to seeing you again.

Enjoy the traditional townscape of Kanazawa retaining its strong trace of wealth of the former Kaga clan, as well as the fusion of modern art and traditional crafts.

Take part in a journey filled with the diverse charms of Japan where tradition, innovation, tranquility and liveliness intersect.
